Debugging Airbnb Clone
There are a few syntax and scoping issues in your JSX. Here’s what stands out: 1. Extra Semicolon and Mismatched Placement of JSX Elements  • You are mapping over spots with Object.values(spots).map(spot => ( … )), and you output a <SpotTile /> component. Immediately after the closing parenthesis of the map, you have a stray semicolon and additional JSX that uses the spot variable. That extra markup is outside of the .map callback, so “spot” isn’t defined in that scope.  • If your intention was to render all that content for each spot, it should all be inside the .map callback inside a single parent element. 2. Mixing Two Patterns  • You’re using a reusable SpotTile component (which you render as <SpotTile … />) and then also including markup (an <img>, spot-info, and spot-actions) that appears to be another tile structure—all within the same render. You need to decide whether to let SpotTile handle all of that display or, if you want to inline the markup, include everything inside the map’s callback. 3. Correcting the JSX Structure  • Remove the stray semicolons that appear after the map callback.  • Wrap all the per-spot markup elements in one parent container (for example, a <div>) inside the map callback.  • Make sure that every reference to spot (like spot.previewImage, spot.name, etc.) is inside that callback so that the variable is defined. Below is one possible corrected version if you want to inline the tile markup instead of using <SpotTile>: --------------------------------------------------- Replace your code with something like this: --------------------------------------------------- import React from 'react'; import OpenModalButton from './OpenModalButton'; import DeleteSpotModal from './DeleteSpotModal'; const ManageSpots = ({ spots, handleCreateNew, handleUpdate, dispatch, fetchUserSpots }) => { return ( <div className="manage-spots-container"> <h1>Manage Your Spots</h1> <button className="create-spot-button" onClick={handleCreateNew}> Create a New Spot </button> <div className="spots-tile"> {Object.values(spots).map(spot => ( <div key={spot.id} className="spot-tile"> <img src={spot.previewImage} alt={spot.name} className="spot-image" /> <div className="spot-info"> <h3>{spot.name}</h3> <p>{spot.city}, {spot.state}</p> <p className="price"><span>${spot.price}</span> night</p> <div className="spot-rating"> <i className="fas fa-star"></i> <span className="stars">{spot.avgRating === 'New' ? 'New' : Number(spot.avgRating).toFixed(1)}</span> </div> </div> <div className="spot-actions"> <button onClick={() => handleUpdate(spot.id)} className="update-button"> Update </button> <OpenModalButton buttonText="Delete" modalComponent={ <DeleteSpotModal spotId={spot.id} onSuccess={() => dispatch(fetchUserSpots())} onError={() => console.error('Failed to delete spot')} /> } /> </div> </div> ))} </div> </div> ); }; export default ManageSpots; --------------------------------------------------- What changed in this version: • All per-spot elements are wrapped in a <div key={spot.id} className="spot-tile">, all inside the map callback. • The stray semicolons have been removed. • Every reference to “spot” is now correctly scoped inside the .map callback. Make sure your component’s props (like spots, handleCreateNew, handleUpdate, dispatch, and fetchUserSpots) are passed correctly from your parent component. This should resolve the errors you’ve been encountering.

Antique Furniture Refurbishing Techniques
Refurbishing antique furniture can be a rewarding process that restores the beauty and functionality of a piece while preserving its historical value. Here are some effective techniques to consider: 1. **Assessment and Planning**: Begin by assessing the condition of the furniture. Identify any damage, such as scratches, stains, or structural issues. Research the piece to understand its historical context and materials used, which will guide your restoration approach. 2. **Cleaning**: Start with a gentle cleaning to remove dirt and grime. Use a mild soap solution and a soft cloth or sponge. Avoid harsh chemicals that could damage the finish or wood. 3. **Repairing Structural Damage**: Address any structural issues first. This might involve gluing loose joints, replacing missing parts, or reinforcing weak areas. Use wood glue and clamps for joints, and try to match any replacement parts to the original materials. 4. **Stripping and Sanding**: If the finish is severely damaged, you may need to strip it. Use a chemical stripper designed for furniture, following safety precautions. After stripping, sand the surface lightly to smooth out imperfections, using fine-grit sandpaper to avoid removing too much material. 5. **Staining and Finishing**: Choose a stain that matches the original color or enhances the wood's natural beauty. Apply the stain evenly and allow it to dry completely. Finish with a protective coat, such as shellac, varnish, or wax, depending on the desired sheen and protection level. 6. **Preserving Patina**: If the piece has a desirable patina, consider preserving it rather than stripping it away. Patina can add character and value to antique furniture. 7. **Upholstery**: For upholstered pieces, consider reupholstering with period-appropriate fabrics. If the original fabric is in good condition, a thorough cleaning might suffice. 8. **Hardware Restoration**: Clean and polish original hardware. If pieces are missing, try to find period-appropriate replacements. Avoid modern hardware that might look out of place. 9. **Documentation**: Keep a record of the restoration process, including any changes made and materials used. This can be valuable for future reference or for potential buyers. 10. **Consultation with Experts**: For valuable or historically significant pieces, consider consulting with a professional restorer to ensure the work is done correctly and the piece's value is maintained. By following these techniques, you can effectively refurbish antique furniture while respecting its history and craftsmanship.

19class ResourceMonitor:
20    def __init__(self):
21        self.metrics_history = deque(maxlen=1000)  # Rolling window of metrics
22        self.process_history = {}  # Historical process data
23        self.dev_process_patterns = [
24            'python', 'node', 'npm', 'java', 'code', 
25            'gcc', 'clang', 'docker', 'git', 'ide'
26        ]
27        self.sampling_interval = 1  # seconds
28        self.is_monitoring = False
29        self.logger = logging.getLogger('ResourceMonitor')
30        
31        # Thresholds for resource alerts
32        self.thresholds = {
33            'cpu_high': 80.0,
34            'memory_high': 85.0,
35            'disk_io_high': 70.0,
36            'process_cpu_high': 50.0
37        }
38
39    async def initialize(self):
40        """Initialize the resource monitor"""
41        self.logger.info("Initializing ResourceMonitor")
42        self.baseline_metrics = await self._establish_baseline()
43        self.is_monitoring = True
44
45    async def _establish_baseline(self) -> Dict:
46        """Establish baseline system metrics"""
47        baseline_samples = []
48        for _ in range(5):  # Collect 5 samples for baseline
49            metrics = await self._collect_single_metric()
50            baseline_samples.append(metrics)
51            await asyncio.sleep(1)
52        
53        return {
54            'cpu_baseline': np.mean([m['cpu'] for m in baseline_samples]),
55            'memory_baseline': np.mean([m['memory'] for m in baseline_samples]),
56            'disk_io_baseline': np.mean([m['disk_io'] for m in baseline_samples])
57        }
58
59    async def collect_metrics(self) -> Dict:
60        """Collect comprehensive system metrics"""
61        try:
62            metrics = await self._collect_single_metric()
63            self.metrics_history.append(metrics)
64            
65            # Analyze for anomalies
66            await self._analyze_metrics(metrics)
67            
68            return metrics
69
70        except Exception as e:
71            self.logger.error(f"Error collecting metrics: {str(e)}")
72            raise
73
74    async def _collect_single_metric(self) -> Dict:
75        """Collect a single set of system metrics"""
76        cpu_metrics = await self._get_cpu_metrics()
77        memory_metrics = self._get_memory_metrics()
78        disk_metrics = await self._get_disk_metrics()
79        process_metrics = await self._get_process_metrics()
80        network_metrics = self._get_network_metrics()
81
82        return {
83            'timestamp': datetime.now().timestamp(),
84            'cpu': cpu_metrics,
85            'memory': memory_metrics,
86            'disk_io': disk_metrics,
87            'processes': process_metrics,
88            'network': network_metrics
89        }
90
91    async def _get_cpu_metrics(self) -> Dict:
92        """Collect detailed CPU metrics"""
93        return {
94            'overall_percent': psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1),
95            'per_cpu_percent': psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1, percpu=True),
96            'load_avg': psutil.getloadavg(),
97            'frequency': psutil.cpu_freq()._asdict() if psutil.cpu_freq() else None,
98            'core_count': psutil.cpu_count(),
99            'core_count_logical': psutil.cpu_count(logical=True)
100        }
101
102    def _get_memory_metrics(self) -> Dict:
103        """Collect detailed memory metrics"""
104        virtual_memory = psutil.virtual_memory()
105        swap_memory = psutil.swap_memory()
106        
107        return {
108            'virtual': {
109                'total': virtual_memory.total,
110                'available': virtual_memory.available,
111                'percent': virtual_memory.percent,
112                'used': virtual_memory.used,
113                'free': virtual_memory.free
114            },
115            'swap': {
116                'total': swap_memory.total,
117                'used': swap_memory.used,
118                'free': swap_memory.free,
119                'percent': swap_memory.percent
120            }
121        }
122
123    async def _get_disk_metrics(self) -> Dict:
124        """Collect detailed disk metrics"""
125        disk_io = psutil.disk_io_counters()
126        disk_usage = {
127            partition.mountpoint: psutil.disk_usage(partition.mountpoint)._asdict()
128            for partition in psutil.disk_partitions()
129            if partition.fstype
130        }
131        
132        return {
133            'io_counters': disk_io._asdict() if disk_io else None,
134            'usage': disk_usage
135        }
136
137    async def _get_process_metrics(self) -> Dict[str, ProcessMetrics]:
138        """Collect metrics for development-related processes"""
139        process_metrics = {}
140        
141        for proc in psutil.process_iter(['pid', 'name', 'cpu_percent', 
142                                       'memory_percent', 'io_counters', 
143                                       'status', 'nice']):
144            try:
145                proc_info = proc.info
146                if any(pattern in proc_info['name'].lower() 
147                      for pattern in self.dev_process_patterns):
148                    
149                    process_metrics[proc_info['pid']] = ProcessMetrics(
150                        pid=proc_info['pid'],
151                        name=proc_info['name'],
152                        cpu_percent=proc_info['cpu_percent'],
153                        memory_percent=proc_info['memory_percent'],
154                        io_counters=proc_info['io_counters']._asdict() 
155                            if proc_info['io_counters'] else None,
156                        status=proc_info['status'],
157                        priority=proc_info['nice']
158                    )
159            except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied, psutil.ZombieProcess):
160                continue
161                
162        return process_metrics
163
164    def _get_network_metrics(self) -> Dict:
165        """Collect network metrics"""
166        network_io = psutil.net_io_counters()
167        connections = len(psutil.net_connections())
168        
169        return {
170            'io_counters': network_io._asdict(),
171            'connection_count': connections
172        }
173
174    async def _analyze_metrics(self, metrics: Dict):
175        """Analyze metrics for anomalies and patterns"""
176        # Check for threshold violations
177        if metrics['cpu']['overall_percent'] > self.thresholds['cpu_high']:
178            await self._handle_high_cpu(metrics)
179            
180        if metrics['memory']['virtual']['percent'] > self.thresholds['memory_high']:
181            await self._handle_high_memory(metrics)
182
183        # Analyze process behavior
184        await self._analyze_process_behavior(metrics['processes'])
185
186    async def _handle_high_cpu(self, metrics: Dict):
187        """Handle high CPU usage scenarios"""
188        self.logger.warning(f"High CPU usage detected: {metrics['cpu']['overall_percent']}%")
189        # Identify CPU-intensive processes
190        high_cpu_processes = [
191            (pid, proc) for pid, proc in metrics['processes'].items()
192            if proc.cpu_percent > self.thresholds['process_cpu_high']
193        ]
194        return high_cpu_processes
195
196    async def _handle_high_memory(self, metrics: Dict):
197        """Handle high memory usage scenarios"""
198        self.logger.warning(f"High memory usage detected: {metrics['memory']['virtual']['percent']}%")
199        # Analyze memory usage patterns
200        return await self._analyze_memory_patterns()
201
202    async def _analyze_process_behavior(self, processes: Dict[str, ProcessMetrics]):
203        """Analyze process behavior patterns"""
204        for pid, process in processes.items():
205            if pid in self.process_history:
206                # Compare with historical data
207                historical_data = self.process_history[pid]
208                await self._detect_process_anomalies(process, historical_data)
209            
210            # Update history
211            self.process_history[pid] = process
212
213    async def get_status(self) -> Dict:
214        """Get current monitoring status"""
215        return {
216            'is_monitoring': self.is_monitoring,
217            'metrics_history_length': len(self.metrics_history),
218            'monitored_processes': len(self.process_history),
219            'baseline_metrics': self.baseline_metrics,
220            'last_metrics': self.metrics_history[-1] if self.metrics_history else None
221        }
222
223    async def cleanup(self):
224        """Cleanup monitoring resources"""
225        self.logger.info("Cleaning up ResourceMonitor")
226        self.is_monitoring = False
227        self.metrics_history.clear()
228        self.process_history.clear()

18class PatternAnalyzer:

55            resource_patterns = await self.analyzers['resource'].analyze(metrics)
56            process_patterns = await self.analyzers['process'].analyze(metrics)
57            workload_patterns = await self.analyzers['workload'].analyze(metrics)

59            # Combine and filter patterns

75class TemporalPatternAnalyzer:
76    """Analyzes temporal patterns in system behavior"""
77    
78    def __init__(self):
79        self.time_series_data = defaultdict(list)
80        self.seasonal_patterns = {}
81
82    async def analyze(self, metrics: Dict) -> List[Pattern]:
83        patterns = []
84        
85        # Daily patterns analysis
86        daily_patterns = self._analyze_daily_patterns(metrics)
87        if daily_patterns:
88            patterns.extend(daily_patterns)
89            
90        # Workload patterns analysis
91        workload_patterns = self._analyze_workload_patterns(metrics)
92        if workload_patterns:
93            patterns.extend(workload_patterns)
94            
95        return patterns
96
97    def _analyze_daily_patterns(self, metrics: Dict) -> List[Pattern]:
98        """Analyze daily usage patterns"""
99        current_hour = datetime.now().hour
100        
101        # Update time series data
102        self.time_series_data[current_hour].append(metrics)
103        
104        if len(self.time_series_data[current_hour]) >= 10:  # Minimum samples
105            cpu_pattern = self._detect_hourly_pattern(
106                'cpu',
107                self.time_series_data[current_hour]
108            )
109            memory_pattern = self._detect_hourly_pattern(
110                'memory',
111                self.time_series_data[current_hour]
112            )
113            
114            return [p for p in [cpu_pattern, memory_pattern] if p]
115        
116        return []
117
118    def _detect_hourly_pattern(self, metric_type: str, samples: List) -> Optional[Pattern]:
119        """Detect patterns in hourly data"""
120        values = [s[metric_type] for s in samples]
121        mean = np.mean(values)
122        std = np.std(values)
123        
124        if std < 0.1 * mean:  # Stable pattern
125            return Pattern(
126                pattern_type=f'stable_{metric_type}',
127                confidence=0.9,
128                metrics={'mean': mean, 'std': std},
129                timestamp=datetime.now(),
130                duration=timedelta(hours=1),
131                impact_score=0.7
132            )
133        return None

143        patterns = []
144        
145        # Update resource history
146        self._update_history(metrics)
147        
148        # Analyze resource correlations
149        correlation_patterns = self._analyze_resource_correlations()
150        if correlation_patterns:

153        # Analyze resource trends
154        trend_patterns = self._analyze_resource_trends()
155        if trend_patterns:
156            patterns.extend(trend_patterns)

160    def _analyze_resource_correlations(self) -> List[Pattern]:
161        """Analyze correlations between different resources"""
162        if len(self.resource_history['cpu']) < 10:
163            return []
164            
165        df = pd.DataFrame(self.resource_history)
166        correlation_matrix = df.corr()
167        
168        patterns = []
169        for i in correlation_matrix.index:
170            for j in correlation_matrix.columns:
171                if i != j and abs(correlation_matrix.loc[i, j]) > 0.8:
172                    patterns.append(Pattern(
173                        pattern_type='resource_correlation',
174                        confidence=abs(correlation_matrix.loc[i, j]),
175                        metrics={'resources': (i, j)},
176                        timestamp=datetime.now(),
177                        duration=timedelta(minutes=30),
178                        impact_score=0.6
179                    ))
180        
181        return patterns

205class WorkloadPatternAnalyzer:
206    """Analyzes patterns in overall system workload"""
207    
208    def __init__(self):
209        self.workload_history = []
210        self.workload_patterns = {}
211
212    async def analyze(self, metrics: Dict) -> List[Pattern]:
213        patterns = []
214        
215        # Update workload history
216        self.workload_history.append(self._calculate_workload_score(metrics))
217        
218        # Analyze workload patterns
219        if len(self.workload_history) >= 10:
220            patterns.extend(self._analyze_workload_trends())
221            patterns.extend(self._analyze_workload_cycles())
222            
223        return patterns
224
225    def _calculate_workload_score(self, metrics: Dict) -> float:
226        """Calculate overall workload score"""
227        cpu_weight = 0.4
228        memory_weight = 0.3
229        io_weight = 0.3
230        
231        return (
232            cpu_weight * metrics['cpu'] +
233            memory_weight * metrics['memory'] +
234            io_weight * metrics['disk_io']
235        )
236
237    def _analyze_workload_trends(self) -> List[Pattern]:
238        """Analyze trends in workload"""
239        recent_workload = self.workload_history[-10:]
240        slope, _, r_value, p_value, _ = stats.linregress(
241            range(len(recent_workload)),
242            recent_workload
243        )
244        
245        if abs(r_value) > 0.8 and p_value < 0.05:
246            return [Pattern(
247                pattern_type='workload_trend',
248                confidence=abs(r_value),
249                metrics={'slope': slope},
250                timestamp=datetime.now(),
251                duration=timedelta(minutes=30),
252                impact_score=0.8
253            )]
254        return []
255
256    def _filter_significant_patterns(self, patterns: List[Pattern]) -> List[Pattern]:
257        """Filter out insignificant patterns"""
258        return [
259            pattern for pattern in patterns
260            if (pattern.confidence >= self.config['min_confidence'] and
261                pattern.impact_score >= self.config['pattern_threshold'])
262        ]
263
264    def _store_patterns(self, patterns: List[Pattern]):
265        """Store patterns for future reference"""
266        for pattern in patterns:
267            self.patterns_db[pattern.pattern_type].append(pattern)
268            
269        # Cleanup old patterns
270        self._cleanup_old_patterns()
271
272    def _cleanup_old_patterns(self):
273        """Remove old patterns from storage"""
274        current_time = datetime.now()
275        for pattern_type in self.patterns_db:
276            self.patterns_db[pattern_type] = [
277                p for p in self.patterns_db[pattern_type]
278                if (current_time - p.timestamp) < timedelta(days=7)
279            ]

1import asyncio
2from typing import Dict, List, Optional
3from enum import Enum
4from dataclasses import dataclass
5import psutil
6import os
7import subprocess
8
9class OptimizationType(Enum):
10    CPU = "cpu"
11    MEMORY = "memory"
12    DISK = "disk"
13    PROCESS = "process"
14    SYSTEM = "system"
15
16@dataclass
17class OptimizationAction:
18    type: OptimizationType
19    priority: int
20    params: Dict
21    expected_impact: float
22    duration: Optional[int] = None
23
24class ResourceOptimizer:
25    def __init__(self):
26        self.logger = logging.getLogger('ResourceOptimizer')
27        self.active_optimizations: Dict[str, OptimizationAction] = {}
28        self.optimization_history: List[Dict] = []
29        self.optimization_locks: Dict[str, asyncio.Lock] = {}
30        
31        # Initialize optimization strategies
32        self.strategies = {
33            OptimizationType.CPU: CPUOptimizer(),
34            OptimizationType.MEMORY: MemoryOptimizer(),
35            OptimizationType.DISK: DiskOptimizer(),
36            OptimizationType.PROCESS: ProcessOptimizer(),
37            OptimizationType.SYSTEM: SystemOptimizer()
38        }
39
40    async def initialize(self):
41        """Initialize the optimizer"""
42        self.logger.info("Initializing ResourceOptimizer")
43        for strategy in self.strategies.values():
44            await strategy.initialize()
45        
46        # Initialize locks for each optimization type
47        for opt_type in OptimizationType:
48            self.optimization_locks[opt_type.value] = asyncio.Lock()
49
50    async def optimize(self, patterns: List[Dict]) -> List[OptimizationAction]:
51        """Generate and apply optimizations based on detected patterns"""
52        try:
53            optimization_actions = await self._generate_optimizations(patterns)
54            valid_actions = self._validate_optimizations(optimization_actions)
55            
56            for action in valid_actions:
57                await self._apply_optimization(action)
58            
59            return valid_actions
60
61        except Exception as e:
62            self.logger.error(f"Optimization error: {str(e)}")
63            return []
64
65    async def _generate_optimizations(self, patterns: List[Dict]) -> List[OptimizationAction]:
66        """Generate optimization actions based on patterns"""
67        optimizations = []
68        
69        for pattern in patterns:
70            strategy = self._select_optimization_strategy(pattern)
71            if strategy:
72                action = await strategy.generate_optimization(pattern)
73                if action:
74                    optimizations.append(action)
75        
76        return optimizations
77
78    def _validate_optimizations(self, actions: List[OptimizationAction]) -> List[OptimizationAction]:
79        """Validate and filter optimization actions"""
80        valid_actions = []
81        
82        for action in actions:
83            if self._is_safe_optimization(action):
84                valid_actions.append(action)
85            else:
86                self.logger.warning(f"Unsafe optimization rejected: {action}")
87        
88        return valid_actions
89
90    async def _apply_optimization(self, action: OptimizationAction):
91        """Apply optimization action with safety checks"""
92        optimization_id = f"{action.type.value}_{datetime.now().timestamp()}"
93        
94        async with self.optimization_locks[action.type.value]:
95            try:
96                # Check if optimization can be applied
97                if not await self._can_apply_optimization(action):
98                    return False
99
100                # Apply optimization through appropriate strategy
101                strategy = self.strategies[action.type]
102                success = await strategy.apply_optimization(action)
103
104                if success:
105                    self.active_optimizations[optimization_id] = action
106                    await self._record_optimization(optimization_id, action)
107                
108                return success
109
110            except Exception as e:
111                self.logger.error(f"Error applying optimization: {str(e)}")
112                return False
113
114class CPUOptimizer:
115    """Handles CPU-specific optimizations"""
116    
117    async def initialize(self):
118        self.cpu_governor = await self._detect_cpu_governor()
119        self.available_frequencies = await self._get_available_frequencies()
120
121    async def generate_optimization(self, pattern: Dict) -> Optional[OptimizationAction]:
122        if pattern['type'] == 'high_cpu_usage':
123            return OptimizationAction(
124                type=OptimizationType.CPU,
125                priority=1,
126                params={'governor': 'powersave'},
127                expected_impact=0.3
128            )
129        return None
130
131    async def apply_optimization(self, action: OptimizationAction) -> bool:
132        try:
133            if 'governor' in action.params:
134                return await self._set_cpu_governor(action.params['governor'])
135            return False
136        except Exception as e:
137            self.logger.error(f"CPU optimization error: {str(e)}")
138            return False
139
140class MemoryOptimizer:
141    """Handles memory-specific optimizations"""
142    
143    async def generate_optimization(self, pattern: Dict) -> Optional[OptimizationAction]:
144        if pattern['type'] == 'memory_pressure':
145            return OptimizationAction(
146                type=OptimizationType.MEMORY,
147                priority=2,
148                params={'drop_caches': True, 'compact_memory': True},
149                expected_impact=0.4
150            )
151        return None
152
153    async def apply_optimization(self, action: OptimizationAction) -> bool:
154        try:
155            if action.params.get('drop_caches'):
156                await self._drop_caches()
157            if action.params.get('compact_memory'):
158                await self._compact_memory()
159            return True
160        except Exception as e:
161            self.logger.error(f"Memory optimization error: {str(e)}")
162            return False
163
164class ProcessOptimizer:
165    """Handles process-specific optimizations"""
166    
167    async def generate_optimization(self, pattern: Dict) -> Optional[OptimizationAction]:
168        if pattern['type'] == 'process_intensive':
169            return OptimizationAction(
170                type=OptimizationType.PROCESS,
171                priority=1,
172                params={
173                    'pid': pattern['pid'],
174                    'nice': 10,
175                    'io_priority': 'idle'
176                },
177                expected_impact=0.25
178            )
179        return None
180
181    async def apply_optimization(self, action: OptimizationAction) -> bool:
182        try:
183            pid = action.params['pid']
184            process = psutil.Process(pid)
185            
186            if 'nice' in action.params:
187                process.nice(action.params['nice'])
188            
189            if 'io_priority' in action.params:
190                self._set_io_priority(pid, action.params['io_priority'])
191            
192            return True
193        except Exception as e:
194            self.logger.error(f"Process optimization error: {str(e)}")
195            return False
196
197class SystemOptimizer:
198    """Handles system-wide optimizations"""
199    
200    async def generate_optimization(self, pattern: Dict) -> Optional[OptimizationAction]:
201        if pattern['type'] == 'system_overload':
202            return OptimizationAction(
203                type=OptimizationType.SYSTEM,
204                priority=3,
205                params={
206                    'swappiness': 10,
207                    'cache_pressure': 50,
208                    'compaction_proactiveness': 1
209                },
210                expected_impact=0.5
211            )
212        return None
213
214    async def apply_optimization(self, action: OptimizationAction) -> bool:
215        try:
216            for param, value in action.params.items():
217                await self._set_sysctl_param(param, value)
218            return True
219        except Exception as e:
220            self.logger.error(f"System optimization error: {str(e)}")
221            return False

Next is the TaskScheduler component, which manages and schedules optimization tasks based on system load and priorities:

Python
1import asyncio
2from typing import Dict, List, Callable, Optional, Any
3from datetime import datetime, timedelta
4from dataclasses import dataclass
5from enum import Enum
6import heapq
7
8class TaskPriority(Enum):
9    CRITICAL = 0
10    HIGH = 1
11    MEDIUM = 2
12    LOW = 3
13
14@dataclass
15class Task:
16    id: str
17    function: Callable
18    priority: TaskPriority
19    args: tuple = ()
20    kwargs: Dict = None
21    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None
22    dependencies: List[str] = None
23    max_retries: int = 3
24    retry_count: int = 0
25    created_at: datetime = None
26    estimated_duration: timedelta = None
27
28class TaskState(Enum):
29    PENDING = "pending"
30    RUNNING = "running"
31    COMPLETED = "completed"
32    FAILED = "failed"
33    CANCELLED = "cancelled"
34
35class TaskScheduler:
36    def __init__(self):
37        self.logger = logging.getLogger('TaskScheduler')
38        self.task_queue = []  # Priority queue
39        self.running_tasks: Dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
40        self.task_history: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
41        self.task_states: Dict[str, TaskState] = {}
42        
43        # Resource thresholds for task execution
44        self.thresholds = {
45            'cpu_max': 80,
46            'memory_max': 85,
47            'concurrent_tasks_max': 5
48        }
49        
50        # Performance metrics
51        self.metrics = {
52            'tasks_completed': 0,
53            'tasks_failed': 0,
54            'average_execution_time': timedelta(0)
55        }
56
57    async def initialize(self):
58        """Initialize the scheduler"""
59        self.logger.info("Initializing TaskScheduler")
60        self._load_configuration()
61        await self._restore_state()
62        self.scheduler_task = asyncio.create_task(self._scheduler_loop())
63
64    async def schedule_task(self, task: Task) -> str:
65        """Schedule a new task"""
66        try:
67            if not task.created_at:
68                task.created_at = datetime.now()
69            
70            # Validate task
71            if not self._validate_task(task):
72                raise ValueError("Invalid task configuration")
73
74            # Add to priority queue
75            heapq.heappush(self.task_queue, (
76                task.priority.value,
77                task.created_at.timestamp(),
78                task
79            ))
80            
81            self.task_states[task.id] = TaskState.PENDING
82            self.logger.info(f"Task scheduled: {task.id}")
83            
84            return task.id
85
86        except Exception as e:
87            self.logger.error(f"Error scheduling task: {str(e)}")
88            raise
89
90    async def _scheduler_loop(self):
91        """Main scheduler loop"""
92        while True:
93            try:
94                await self._process_next_task()
95                await asyncio.sleep(1)  # Prevent CPU hogging
96            except Exception as e:
97                self.logger.error(f"Scheduler loop error: {str(e)}")
98                await asyncio.sleep(5)  # Error backoff
99
100    async def _process_next_task(self):
101        """Process the next task in queue"""
102        if not self.task_queue:
103            return
104
105        if not await self._can_execute_task():
106            return
107
108        # Get next task
109        _, _, task = heapq.heappop(self.task_queue)
110
111        # Check dependencies
112        if not await self._check_dependencies(task):
113            heapq.heappush(self.task_queue, (task.priority.value, 
114                                           task.created_at.timestamp(), 
115                                           task))
116            return
117
118        # Execute task
119        await self._execute_task(task)
120
121    async def _execute_task(self, task: Task):
122        """Execute a task"""
123        self.task_states[task.id] = TaskState.RUNNING
124        start_time = datetime.now()
125
126        try:
127            # Create task execution context
128            context = self._create_execution_context(task)
129            
130            # Execute task with timeout
131            async with context:
132                task_coroutine = task.function(*task.args, **(task.kwargs or {}))
133                running_task = asyncio.create_task(task_coroutine)
134                self.running_tasks[task.id] = running_task
135
136                try:
137                    await asyncio.wait_for(
138                        running_task,
139                        timeout=self._get_timeout(task)
140                    )
141                    self._handle_task_completion(task, start_time)
142                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
143                    await self._handle_task_timeout(task)
144
145        except Exception as e:
146            await self._handle_task_failure(task, e)
147
148    async def _can_execute_task(self) -> bool:
149        """Check if system can execute more tasks"""
150        cpu_usage = psutil.cpu_percent()
151        memory_usage = psutil.virtual_memory().percent
152        running_tasks = len(self.running_tasks)
153
154        return (
155            cpu_usage < self.thresholds['cpu_max'] and
156            memory_usage < self.thresholds['memory_max'] and
157            running_tasks < self.thresholds['concurrent_tasks_max']
158        )
159
160    async def _check_dependencies(self, task: Task) -> bool:
161        """Check if task dependencies are met"""
162        if not task.dependencies:
163            return True
164
165        for dep_id in task.dependencies:
166            if (dep_id not in self.task_states or
167                self.task_states[dep_id] != TaskState.COMPLETED):
168                return False
169        return True
170
171    def _create_execution_context(self, task: Task):
172        """Create context for task execution"""
173        return TaskExecutionContext(
174            task=task,
175            scheduler=self,
176            logger=self.logger
177        )
178
179    async def _handle_task_failure(self, task: Task, error: Exception):
180        """Handle task failure"""
181        self.logger.error(f"Task {task.id} failed: {str(error)}")
182        
183        if task.retry_count < task.max_retries:
184            task.retry_count += 1
185            await self.schedule_task(task)
186        else:
187            self.task_states[task.id] = TaskState.FAILED
188            self.metrics['tasks_failed'] += 1
189
190    async def _handle_task_timeout(self, task: Task):
191        """Handle task timeout"""
192        self.logger.warning(f"Task {task.id} timed out")
193        if task.id in self.running_tasks:
194            self.running_tasks[task.id].cancel()
195            del self.running_tasks[task.id]
196        
197        await self._handle_task_failure(task, TimeoutError("Task timed out"))
198
199    def _handle_task_completion(self, task: Task, start_time: datetime):
200        """Handle successful task completion"""
201        execution_time = datetime.now() - start_time
202        self.task_states[task.id] = TaskState.COMPLETED
203        self.metrics['tasks_completed'] += 1
204        
205        # Update average execution time
206        self.metrics['average_execution_time'] = (
207            self.metrics['average_execution_time'] + 
208            (execution_time - self.metrics['average_execution_time']) / 
209            self.metrics['tasks_completed']
210        )
211
212        self._update_task_history(task, execution_time)
213
214    def _update_task_history(self, task: Task, execution_time: timedelta):
215        """Update task execution history"""
216        self.task_history[task.id] = {
217            'task': task,
218            'execution_time': execution_time,
219            'completed_at': datetime.now(),
220            'state': TaskState.COMPLETED
221        }
222
223    async def get_task_status(self, task_id: str) -> Dict:
224        """Get status of a specific task"""
225        return {
226            'state': self.task_states.get(task_id),
227            'history': self.task_history.get(task_id),
228            'is_running': task_id in self.running_tasks
229        }
230
231    async def cancel_task(self, task_id: str) -> bool:
232        """Cancel a scheduled or running task"""
233        try:
234            # Cancel if running
235            if task_id in self.running_tasks:
236                self.running_tasks[task_id].cancel()
237                del self.running_tasks[task_id]
238            
239            # Remove from queue if pending
240            self.task_queue = [
241                (p, t, task) for p, t, task in self.task_queue 
242                if task.id != task_id
243            ]
244            heapq.heapify(self.task_queue)
245            
246            self.task_states[task_id] = TaskState.CANCELLED
247            return True
248
249        except Exception as e:
250            self.logger.error(f"Error cancelling task {task_id}: {str(e)}")
251            return False
252
253    async def get_scheduler_stats(self) -> Dict:
254        """Get scheduler statistics"""
255        return {
256            'pending_tasks': len(self.task_queue),
257            'running_tasks': len(self.running_tasks),
258            'completed_tasks': self.metrics['tasks_completed'],
259            'failed_tasks': self.metrics['tasks_failed'],
260            'average_execution_time': self.metrics['average_execution_time'],
261            'system_load': {
262                'cpu': psutil.cpu_percent(),
263                'memory': psutil.virtual_memory().percent
264            }
265        }
266
267class TaskExecutionContext:
268    """Context manager for task execution"""
269    
270    def __init__(self, task: Task, scheduler: 'TaskScheduler', logger):
271        self.task = task
272        self.scheduler = scheduler
273        self.logger = logger
274
275    async def __aenter__(self):
276        self.logger.debug(f"Starting execution of task {self.task.id}")
277        return self
278
279    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
280        if exc_type is not None:
281            self.logger.error(f"Task {self.task.id} failed: {str(exc_val)}")
282        if self.task.id in self.scheduler.running_tasks:
283            del self.scheduler.running_tasks[self.task.id]

Key Features of the TaskScheduler:

  • Multiple priority levels

1import json
2import yaml
3from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
4from pathlib import Path
5import asyncio
6from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
7from watchdog.observers import Observer
8from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler
9
10@dataclass
11class SystemConfig:
12    sampling_rate: int = 5
13    history_size: int = 1000
14    log_level: str = "INFO"
15    max_cpu_usage: float = 80.0
16    max_memory_usage: float = 85.0
17    optimization_threshold: float = 0.8
18    backup_enabled: bool = True
19    auto_tune: bool = True
20
21@dataclass
22class UserPreferences:
23    priority_processes: list = None
24    ignored_processes: list = None
25    quiet_hours: Dict[str, str] = None
26    optimization_aggressiveness: float = 0.5
27    notification_level: str = "IMPORTANT"
28
29class ConfigManager:
30    def __init__(self, config_path: str = "config"):
31        self.logger = logging.getLogger('ConfigManager')
32        self.config_path = Path(config_path)
33        self.config_file = self.config_path / "system_config.yaml"
34        self.preferences_file = self.config_path / "user_preferences.yaml"
35        
36        # Initialize configurations
37        self.system_config = SystemConfig()
38        self.user_preferences = UserPreferences()
39        
40        # Configuration locks
41        self.config_lock = asyncio.Lock()
42        
43        # Change tracking
44        self.pending_changes: Dict[str, Any] = {}
45        self.last_modified = {}
46        
47        # Setup file watching
48        self.observer = Observer()
49        self.setup_file_watching()
50
51    async def initialize(self):
52        """Initialize configuration manager"""
53        try:
54            self.logger.info("Initializing ConfigManager")
55            
56            # Create config directory if it doesn't exist
57            self.config_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
58            
59            # Load configurations
60            await self.load_configurations()
61            
62            # Start file watching
63            self.start_file_watching()
64            
65            # Initialize adaptive config
66            await self.initialize_adaptive_config()
67            
68        except Exception as e:
69            self.logger.error(f"Configuration initialization error: {str(e)}")
70            raise
71
72    async def load_configurations(self):
73        """Load all configurations"""
74        async with self.config_lock:
75            try:
76                # Load system configuration
77                if self.config_file.exists():
78                    with open(self.config_file) as f:
79                        system_config = yaml.safe_load(f)
80                        self.system_config = SystemConfig(**system_config)
81                else:
82                    await self.save_system_config()
83
84                # Load user preferences
85                if self.preferences_file.exists():
86                    with open(self.preferences_file) as f:
87                        user_prefs = yaml.safe_load(f)
88                        self.user_preferences = UserPreferences(**user_prefs)
89                else:
90                    await self.save_user_preferences()
91
92            except Exception as e:
93                self.logger.error(f"Error loading configurations: {str(e)}")
94                raise
95
96    async def save_system_config(self):
97        """Save system configuration"""
98        async with self.config_lock:
99            try:
100                with open(self.config_file, 'w') as f:
101                    yaml.safe_dump(asdict(self.system_config), f)
102                self.last_modified['system_config'] = datetime.now()
103            except Exception as e:
104                self.logger.error(f"Error saving system config: {str(e)}")
105                raise
106
107    async def save_user_preferences(self):
108        """Save user preferences"""
109        async with self.config_lock:
110            try:
111                with open(self.preferences_file, 'w') as f:
112                    yaml.safe_dump(asdict(self.user_preferences), f)
113                self.last_modified['user_preferences'] = datetime.now()
114            except Exception as e:
115                self.logger.error(f"Error saving user preferences: {str(e)}")
116                raise
117
118    def setup_file_watching(self):
119        """Setup file system watching for config files"""
120        class ConfigFileHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
121            def __init__(self, config_manager):
122                self.config_manager = config_manager
123
124            def on_modified(self, event):
125                if not event.is_directory:
126                    if event.src_path.endswith('system_config.yaml'):
127                        asyncio.create_task(
128                            self.config_manager.handle_config_change('system_config')
129                        )
130                    elif event.src_path.endswith('user_preferences.yaml'):
131                        asyncio.create_task(
132                            self.config_manager.handle_config_change('user_preferences')
133                        )
134
135        self.observer.schedule(
136            ConfigFileHandler(self),
137            str(self.config_path),
138            recursive=False
139        )
140
141    def start_file_watching(self):
142        """Start file system observer"""
143        self.observer.start()
144
145    async def handle_config_change(self, config_type: str):
146        """Handle configuration file changes"""
147        try:
148            async with self.config_lock:
149                if config_type == 'system_config':
150                    await self.load_configurations()
151                    await self.apply_system_config_changes()
152                elif config_type == 'user_preferences':
153                    await self.load_configurations()
154                    await self.apply_user_preference_changes()
155                
156                # Notify subscribers
157                await self.notify_config_changes(config_type)
158                
159        except Exception as e:
160            self.logger.error(f"Error handling config change: {str(e)}")
161
162    async def apply_system_config_changes(self):
163        """Apply changes in system configuration"""
164        try:
165            # Apply sampling rate changes
166            if 'sampling_rate' in self.pending_changes:
167                await self.update_sampling_rate(
168                    self.pending_changes['sampling_rate']
169                )
170            
171            # Apply other system changes
172            for key, value in self.pending_changes.items():
173                if hasattr(self.system_config, key):
174                    setattr(self.system_config, key, value)
175            
176            self.pending_changes.clear()
177            
178        except Exception as e:
179            self.logger.error(f"Error applying system config changes: {str(e)}")
180            raise
181
182    async def initialize_adaptive_config(self):
183        """Initialize adaptive configuration system"""
184        self.adaptive_config = {
185            'performance_metrics': {},
186            'optimization_history': [],
187            'system_patterns': {},
188            'adaptation_rules': self._load_adaptation_rules()
189        }
190
191    def _load_adaptation_rules(self) -> Dict:
192        """Load adaptation rules for adaptive configuration"""
193        return {
194            'cpu_intensive': {
195                'condition': lambda metrics: metrics['cpu_usage'] > 75,
196                'actions': [
197                    ('sampling_rate', 'increase'),
198                    ('optimization_threshold', 'decrease')
199                ]
200            },
201            'memory_intensive': {
202                'condition': lambda metrics: metrics['memory_usage'] > 80,
203                'actions': [
204                    ('optimization_threshold', 'decrease'),
205                    ('backup_enabled', False)
206                ]
207            }
208        }
209
210    async def update_adaptive_config(self, metrics: Dict):
211        """Update adaptive configuration based on system metrics"""
212        try:
213            for rule_name, rule in self.adaptive_config['adaptation_rules'].items():
214                if rule['condition'](metrics):
215                    await self._apply_adaptation_rule(rule['actions'])
216        except Exception as e:
217            self.logger.error(f"Error updating adaptive config: {str(e)}")
218
219    async def _apply_adaptation_rule(self, actions: list):
220        """Apply adaptation rule actions"""
221        async with self.config_lock:
222            for param, action in actions:
223                if hasattr(self.system_config, param):
224                    current_value = getattr(self.system_config, param)
225                    new_value = self._calculate_adapted_value(
226                        param, current_value, action
227                    )
228                    setattr(self.system_config, param, new_value)
229            
230            await self.save_system_config()
231
232    def _calculate_adapted_value(self, param: str, current_value: Any, action: str) -> Any:
233        """Calculate new value based on adaptation action"""
234        if isinstance(current_value, (int, float)):
235            if action == 'increase':
236                return current_value * 1.2
237            elif action == 'decrease':
238                return current_value * 0.8
239        elif isinstance(current_value, bool):
240            return action if isinstance(action, bool) else current_value
241        return current_value
242
243    async def get_config(self, config_type: str) -> Dict:
244        """Get current configuration"""
245        async with self.config_lock:
246            if config_type == 'system':
247                return asdict(self.system_config)
248            elif config_type == 'user':
249                return asdict(self.user_preferences)
250            elif config_type == 'adaptive':
251                return self.adaptive_config
252            else:
253                raise ValueError(f"Unknown config type: {config_type}")
254
255    async def update_config(self, config_type: str, updates: Dict):
256        """Update configuration"""
257        async with self.config_lock:
258            try:
259                if config_type == 'system':
260                    for key, value in updates.items():
261                        if hasattr(self.system_config, key):
262                            setattr(self.system_config, key, value)
263                    await self.save_system_config()
264                
265                elif config_type == 'user':
266                    for key, value in updates.items():
267                        if hasattr(self.user_preferences, key):
268                            setattr(self.user_preferences, key, value)
269                    await self.save_user_preferences()
270                
271                await self.notify_config_changes(config_type)
272                
273            except Exception as e:
274                self.logger.error(f"Error updating config: {str(e)}")
275                raise
276
277    async def notify_config_changes(self, config_type: str):
278        """Notify subscribers of configuration changes"""
279        # Implementation depends on your event system
280        pass

9
10class NotificationPriority(Enum):

16class NotificationType(Enum):

35class NotificationManager:

39        self.notification_queue = asyncio.Queue()
40        self.subscribers: Dict[str, List[callable]] = {}
41        self.notification_history: List[Notification] = []
42        
43        # Notification settings
44        self.settings = {
45            'max_history': 1000,
46            'batch_size': 10,
47            'notification_timeout': 300,  # seconds
48            'enable_external_notifications': False
49        }
50        
51        # Initialize notification handlers
52        self.handlers = {
53            NotificationType.SYSTEM: self._handle_system_notification,
54            NotificationType.OPTIMIZATION: self._handle_optimization_notification,
55            NotificationType.PERFORMANCE: self._handle_performance_notification,
56            NotificationType.SECURITY: self._handle_security_notification,
57            NotificationType.USER: self._handle_user_notification
58        }
59
60    async def initialize(self):
61        """Initialize the notification manager"""
62        self.logger.info("Initializing NotificationManager")
63        
64        # Start notification processor
65        self.processor_task = asyncio.create_task(self._process_notifications())
66        
67        # Initialize external notification services
68        if self.settings['enable_external_notifications']:
69            await self._initialize_external_services()
70
71    async def send_notification(self, 
72                              notification_type: NotificationType,
73                              message: str,
74                              priority: NotificationPriority = NotificationPriority.NORMAL,
75                              details: Dict = None) -> str:
76        """Send a new notification"""
77        try:
78            notification = Notification(
79                id=self._generate_notification_id(),
80                type=notification_type,
81                priority=priority,
82                message=message,
83                timestamp=datetime.now(),
84                details=details
85            )
86            
87            await self.notification_queue.put(notification)
88            self.notifications[notification.id] = notification
89            
90            # Log critical notifications
91            if priority == NotificationPriority.CRITICAL:
92                self.logger.critical(f"Critical notification: {message}")
93            
94            return notification.id
95
96        except Exception as e:
97            self.logger.error(f"Error sending notification: {str(e)}")
98            raise
99
100    async def _process_notifications(self):
101        """Process notifications from the queue"""
102        while True:
103            try:
104                # Process notifications in batches
105                notifications = []
106                try:
107                    while len(notifications) < self.settings['batch_size']:
108                        notification = await asyncio.wait_for(
109                            self.notification_queue.get(),
110                            timeout=0.1
111                        )
112                        notifications.append(notification)
113                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
114                    pass
115
116                if notifications:
117                    await self._handle_notifications_batch(notifications)
118
119            except Exception as e:
120                self.logger.error(f"Error processing notifications: {str(e)}")
121                await asyncio.sleep(5)  # Error backoff
122
123    async def _handle_notifications_batch(self, notifications: List[Notification]):
124        """Handle a batch of notifications"""
125        for notification in notifications:
126            try:
127                # Process notification through appropriate handler
128                handler = self.handlers.get(notification.type)
129                if handler:
130                    await handler(notification)
131
132                # Update notification history
133                self._update_history(notification)
134
135                # Notify subscribers
136                await self._notify_subscribers(notification)
137
138            except Exception as e:
139                self.logger.error(f"Error handling notification {notification.id}: {str(e)}")
140
141    async def _handle_system_notification(self, notification: Notification):
142        """Handle system notifications"""
143        if notification.priority in [NotificationPriority.CRITICAL, NotificationPriority.HIGH]:
144            await self._send_urgent_alert(notification)
145        
146        if notification.action_required:
147            await self._create_system_action(notification)
148
149    async def _handle_optimization_notification(self, notification: Notification):
150        """Handle optimization notifications"""
151        if notification.details and 'optimization_type' in notification.details:
152            await self._log_optimization_event(notification)
153            
154        if notification.priority == NotificationPriority.CRITICAL:
155            await self._handle_critical_optimization(notification)
156
157    async def _handle_performance_notification(self, notification: Notification):
158        """Handle performance notifications"""
159        await self._log_performance_metrics(notification)
160        
161        if notification.details and 'threshold_exceeded' in notification.details:
162            await self._handle_performance_threshold(notification)
163
164    async def _handle_security_notification(self, notification: Notification):
165        """Handle security notifications"""
166        # Always treat security notifications as high priority
167        notification.priority = NotificationPriority.HIGH
168        await self._send_urgent_alert(notification)
169        await self._log_security_event(notification)
170
171    async def _handle_user_notification(self, notification: Notification):
172        """Handle user notifications"""
173        if self.settings['enable_external_notifications']:
174            await self._send_external_notification(notification)
175        
176        await self._update_user_notification_preferences(notification)
177
178    async def subscribe(self, notification_type: NotificationType, callback: callable):
179        """Subscribe to notifications"""
180        if notification_type not in self.subscribers:
181            self.subscribers[notification_type] = []
182        self.subscribers[notification_type].append(callback)
183
184    async def unsubscribe(self, notification_type: NotificationType, callback: callable):
185        """Unsubscribe from notifications"""
186        if notification_type in self.subscribers:
187            self.subscribers[notification_type].remove(callback)
188
189    async def acknowledge_notification(self, notification_id: str):
190        """Acknowledge a notification"""
191        if notification_id in self.notifications:
192            self.notifications[notification_id].acknowledged = True
193            await self._update_notification_status(notification_id)
194
195    async def get_notifications(self, 
196                              notification_type: Optional[NotificationType] = None,
197                              priority: Optional[NotificationPriority] = None,
198                              limit: int = 100) -> List[Notification]:
199        """Get notifications with optional filtering"""
200        notifications = list(self.notifications.values())
201        
202        if notification_type:
203            notifications = [n for n in notifications if n.type == notification_type]
204        
205        if priority:
206            notifications = [n for n in notifications if n.priority == priority]
207        
208        return sorted(
209            notifications,
210            key=lambda x: x.timestamp,
211            reverse=True
212        )[:limit]
213
214    async def _send_urgent_alert(self, notification: Notification):
215        """Send urgent alerts through all available channels"""
216        try:
217            # Log urgent alert
218            self.logger.warning(f"Urgent alert: {notification.message}")
219            
220            # Send external notifications if enabled
221            if self.settings['enable_external_notifications']:
222                await self._send_external_notification(notification)
223            
224            # Create system alert
225            await self._create_system_alert(notification)
226            
227        except Exception as e:
228            self.logger.error(f"Error sending urgent alert: {str(e)}")
229
230    def _update_history(self, notification: Notification):
231        """Update notification history"""
232        self.notification_history.append(notification)
233        
234        # Maintain history size limit
235        while len(self.notification_history) > self.settings['max_history']:
236            self.notification_history.pop(0)
237
238    async def _notify_subscribers(self, notification: Notification):
239        """Notify subscribers of new notifications"""
240        if notification.type in self.subscribers:
241            for callback in self.subscribers[notification.type]:
242                try:
243                    await callback(notification)
244                except Exception as e:
245                    self.logger.error(f"Error in subscriber callback: {str(e)}")
246
247    def _generate_notification_id(self) -> str:
248        """Generate unique notification ID"""
249        return f"notif_{datetime.now().timestamp()}_{id(datetime.now())}"
250
251    async def cleanup(self):
252        """Cleanup notification manager resources"""
253        self.logger.info("Cleaning up NotificationManager")
254        self.processor_task.cancel()
255        
256        try:
257            await self.processor_task
258        except asyncio.CancelledError:
259            pass
260        
261        # Clear queues and history
262        self.notifications.clear()
263        self.notification_history.clear()

Key Features of the NotificationManager:

  1. Notification Types and Priorities
  • Multiple notification categories
  • Priority levels
  • Action-required notifications
  • Acknowledgment system
  1. Notification Processing
  • Asynchronous processing
  • Batch processing
  • Queue management
  • History tracking
  1. Notification Handlers
  • Type-specific handlers
  • External notification support
  • Urgent alert system
  • Security event handling
  1. Subscription System
  • Type-based subscriptions
  • Callback management
  • Notification filtering
  • Real-time updates
  1. History and Status Management
  • Notification history
  • Status tracking
  • Acknowledgment system
  • Cleanup procedures

Next is the MetricsCollector component, which handles gathering, aggregating, and analyzing system performance metrics. This component works closely with the ResourceMonitor but focuses on long-term metrics collection and analysis:

Python
1import asyncio
2from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union
3from datetime import datetime, timedelta
4import numpy as np
5import pandas as pd
6from dataclasses import dataclass
7import psutil
8import sqlite3
9import aiosqlite
10from collections import deque
11
12@dataclass
13class MetricPoint:
14    timestamp: datetime
15    metric_type: str
16    value: float
17    tags: Dict[str, str]
18    source: str
19
20class MetricsAggregation:
21    def __init__(self):
22        self.count: int = 0
23        self.sum: float = 0.0
24        self.min: float = float('inf')
25        self.max: float = float('-inf')
26        self.mean: float = 0.0
27        self.variance: float = 0.0
28
29class MetricsCollector:
30    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "metrics.db"):
31        self.logger = logging.getLogger('MetricsCollector')
32        self.db_path = db_path
33        
34        # In-memory buffers
35        self.metric_buffer = deque(maxlen=1000)
36        self.aggregation_cache = {}
37        
38        # Metric definitions
39        self.metric_definitions = self._initialize_metric_definitions()
40        
41        # Collection intervals
42        self.collection_intervals = {
43            'high_frequency': 1,    # 1 second
44            'normal': 5,           # 5 seconds
45            'low_frequency': 60    # 1 minute
46        }
47        
48        # Initialize statistical trackers
49        self.statistical_trackers = {}
50
51    async def initialize(self):
52        """Initialize the metrics collector"""
53        try:
54            self.logger.info("Initializing MetricsCollector")
55            
56            # Initialize database
57            await self._initialize_database()
58            
59            # Start collection tasks
60            self.collection_tasks = {
61                'high_freq': asyncio.create_task(self._collect_high_frequency_metrics()),
62                'normal': asyncio.create_task(self._collect_normal_metrics()),
63                'low_freq': asyncio.create_task(self._collect_low_frequency_metrics())
64            }
65            
66            # Initialize statistical tracking
67            await self._initialize_statistical_tracking()
68
69        except Exception as e:
70            self.logger.error(f"Initialization error: {str(e)}")
71            raise
72
73    def _initialize_metric_definitions(self) -> Dict:
74        """Initialize metric definitions and collection rules"""
75        return {
76            'cpu_usage': {
77                'type': 'gauge',
78                'frequency': 'high_frequency',
79                'aggregation': ['avg', 'max'],
80                'alert_threshold': 80.0
81            },
82            'memory_usage': {
83                'type': 'gauge',
84                'frequency': 'high_frequency',
85                'aggregation': ['avg', 'max'],
86                'alert_threshold': 85.0
87            },
88            'disk_io': {
89                'type': 'counter',
90                'frequency': 'normal',
91                'aggregation': ['sum', 'rate'],
92                'alert_threshold': None
93            },
94            'process_count': {
95                'type': 'gauge',
96                'frequency': 'normal',
97                'aggregation': ['avg'],
98                'alert_threshold': None
99            },
100            'network_throughput': {
101                'type': 'counter',
102                'frequency': 'high_frequency',
103                'aggregation': ['sum', 'rate'],
104                'alert_threshold': None
105            }
106        }
107
108    async def _initialize_database(self):
109        """Initialize SQLite database for metrics storage"""
110        async with aiosqlite.connect(self.db_path) as db:
111            await db.execute('''
112                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS metrics (
113                    timestamp DATETIME,
114                    metric_type TEXT,
115                    value REAL,
116                    tags TEXT,
117                    source TEXT
118                )
119            ''')
120            
121            await db.execute('''
122                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS aggregations (
123                    timestamp DATETIME,
124                    metric_type TEXT,
125                    aggregation_type TEXT,
126                    value REAL,
127                    period TEXT
128                )
129            ''')
130            
131            await db.commit()
132
133    async def collect_metric(self, 
134                           metric_type: str, 
135                           value: float, 
136                           tags: Dict[str, str] = None,
137                           source: str = "system"):
138        """Collect a single metric point"""
139        try:
140            metric = MetricPoint(
141                timestamp=datetime.now(),
142                metric_type=metric_type,
143                value=value,
144                tags=tags or {},
145                source=source
146            )
147            
148            # Add to buffer
149            self.metric_buffer.append(metric)
150            
151            # Process metric
152            await self._process_metric(metric)
153            
154            # Check for alerts
155            await self._check_alert_threshold(metric)
156
157        except Exception as e:
158            self.logger.error(f"Error collecting metric: {str(e)}")
159
160    async def _process_metric(self, metric: MetricPoint):
161        """Process a single metric point"""
162        try:
163            # Update statistical trackers
164            self._update_statistics(metric)
165            
166            # Store metric
167            await self._store_metric(metric)
168            
169            # Update aggregations
170            await self._update_aggregations(metric)
171
172        except Exception as e:
173            self.logger.error(f"Error processing metric: {str(e)}")
174
175    async def _collect_high_frequency_metrics(self):
176        """Collect high-frequency metrics"""
177        while True:
178            try:
179                # Collect CPU metrics
180                cpu_usage = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1)
181                await self.collect_metric('cpu_usage', cpu_usage)
182                
183                # Collect memory metrics
184                memory = psutil.virtual_memory()
185                await self.collect_metric('memory_usage', memory.percent)
186                
187                # Collect network metrics
188                network = psutil.net_io_counters()
189                await self.collect_metric('network_throughput', 
190                                        network.bytes_sent + network.bytes_recv)
191                
192                await asyncio.sleep(self.collection_intervals['high_frequency'])
193
194            except Exception as e:
195                self.logger.error(f"Error collecting high-frequency metrics: {str(e)}")
196                await asyncio.sleep(5)
197
198    async def _store_metric(self, metric: MetricPoint):
199        """Store metric in database"""
200        async with aiosqlite.connect(self.db_path) as db:
201            await db.execute('''
202                INSERT INTO metrics 
203                (timestamp, metric_type, value, tags, source)
204                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
205            ''', (
206                metric.timestamp,
207                metric.metric_type,
208                metric.value,
209                json.dumps(metric.tags),
210                metric.source
211            ))
212            await db.commit()
213
214    async def _update_aggregations(self, metric: MetricPoint):
215        """Update metric aggregations"""
216        metric_def = self.metric_definitions.get(metric.metric_type)
217        if not metric_def:
218            return
219
220        for agg_type in metric_def['aggregation']:
221            key = f"{metric.metric_type}_{agg_type}"
222            if key not in self.aggregation_cache:
223                self.aggregation_cache[key] = MetricsAggregation()
224
225            agg = self.aggregation_cache[key]
226            self._update_aggregation(agg, metric.value)
227
228    def _update_aggregation(self, agg: MetricsAggregation, value: float):
229        """Update aggregation calculations"""
230        agg.count += 1
231        agg.sum += value
232        agg.min = min(agg.min, value)
233        agg.max = max(agg.max, value)
234        
235        # Update running mean and variance using Welford's algorithm
236        delta = value - agg.mean
237        agg.mean += delta / agg.count
238        delta2 = value - agg.mean
239        agg.variance += delta * delta2
240
241    async def get_metrics(self,
242                         metric_type: str,
243                         start_time: datetime,
244                         end_time: datetime = None,
245                         aggregation: str = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
246        """Retrieve metrics with optional aggregation"""
247        try:
248            query = '''
249                SELECT timestamp, value, tags
250                FROM metrics
251                WHERE metric_type = ?
252                AND timestamp >= ?
253            '''
254            params = [metric_type, start_time]
255            
256            if end_time:
257                query += ' AND timestamp <= ?'
258                params.append(end_time)
259                
260            async with aiosqlite.connect(self.db_path) as db:
261                async with db.execute(query, params) as cursor:
262                    rows = await cursor.fetchall()
263                    
264            df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['timestamp', 'value', 'tags'])
265            
266            if aggregation:
267                return self._aggregate_metrics(df, aggregation)
268            
269            return df
270
271        except Exception as e:
272            self.logger.error(f"Error retrieving metrics: {str(e)}")
273            raise
274
275    def _aggregate_metrics(self, df: pd.DataFrame, aggregation: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
276        """Aggregate metrics based on specified function"""
277        if aggregation == 'avg':
278            return df.groupby('timestamp').value.mean().reset_index()
279        elif aggregation == 'sum':
280            return df.groupby('timestamp').value.sum().reset_index()
281        elif aggregation == 'max':
282            return df.groupby('timestamp').value.max().reset_index()
283        elif aggregation == 'min':
284            return df.groupby('timestamp').value.min().reset_index()
285        else:
286            raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation type: {aggregation}")
287
288    async def get_statistics(self, 
289                           metric_type: str, 
290                           period: str = '1h') -> Dict:
291        """Get statistical information for a metric"""
292        try:
293            end_time = datetime.now()
294            start_time = end_time - self._parse_period(period)
295            
296            df = await self.get_metrics(metric_type, start_time, end_time)
297            
298            return {
299                'mean': df.value.mean(),
300                'std': df.value.std(),
301                'min': df.value.min(),
302                'max': df.value.max(),
303                'count': len(df),
304                'last_value': df.value.iloc[-1] if not df.empty else None
305            }
306
307        except Exception as e:
308            self.logger.error(f"Error calculating statistics: {str(e)}")
309            raise
310
311    def _parse_period(self, period: str) -> timedelta:
312        """Parse period string into timedelta"""
313        unit = period[-1]
314        value = int(period[:-1])
315        
316        if unit == 'h':
317            return timedelta(hours=value)
318        elif unit == 'd':
319            return timedelta(days=value)
320        elif unit == 'm':
321            return timedelta(minutes=value)
322        else:
323            raise ValueError(f"Invalid period format: {period}")
324
325    async def cleanup(self):
326        """Cleanup metrics collector resources"""
327        self.logger.info("Cleaning up MetricsCollector")
328        
329        # Cancel collection tasks
330        for task in self.collection_tasks.values():
331            task.cancel()
332            
333        try:
334            await asyncio.gather(*self.collection_tasks.values())
335        except asyncio.CancelledError:
336            pass
337        
338        # Cleanup database
339        await self._cleanup_old_metrics()
340
341    async def _cleanup_old_metrics(self):
342        """Clean up old metrics from database"""
343        retention_period = timedelta(days=30)
344        cleanup_time = datetime.now() - retention_period
345        
346        async with aiosqlite.connect(self.db_path) as db:
347            await db.execute('''
348                DELETE FROM metrics
349                WHERE timestamp < ?
350            ''', (cleanup_time,))
351            await db.commit()

9class HealthStatus(Enum):

26class SystemHealthMonitor:

36            'disk': DiskHealthMonitor(),

42        self.anomaly_detector = AnomalyDetector()

44        # Prediction models

49            'fast': 10,    # 10 seconds
50            'normal': 30,  # 30 seconds
51            'slow': 300    # 5 minutes
52        }
53
54    async def initialize(self):
55        """Initialize the health monitor"""
56        try:
57            self.logger.info("Initializing SystemHealthMonitor")
58            
59            # Initialize component monitors
60            for monitor in self.monitors.values():
61                await monitor.initialize()
62            
63            # Initialize anomaly detector
64            await self.anomaly_detector.initialize()

66            # Start health check tasks
67            self.health_tasks = {
68                'fast': asyncio.create_task(self._run_fast_health_checks()),
69                'normal': asyncio.create_task(self._run_normal_health_checks()),
70                'slow': asyncio.create_task(self._run_slow_health_checks())
71            }
72            
73            # Initialize predictive models
74            await self._initialize_predictive_models()
75
76        except Exception as e:
77            self.logger.error(f"Initialization error: {str(e)}")
78            raise
79
80    async def _run_fast_health_checks(self):
81        """Run high-frequency health checks"""
82        while True:
83            try:
84                # Check CPU and Memory
85                await self._check_cpu_health()
86                await self._check_memory_health()
87                
88                # Update real-time metrics
89                await self._update_realtime_metrics()
90                
91                await asyncio.sleep(self.check_intervals['fast'])
92
93            except Exception as e:
94                self.logger.error(f"Error in fast health checks: {str(e)}")
95                await asyncio.sleep(5)
96
97    async def _check_cpu_health(self) -> HealthMetric:
98        """Check CPU health status"""
99        try:
100            cpu_metrics = await self.monitors['cpu'].get_health_metrics()
101            status = self._determine_health_status(cpu_metrics)
102            
103            metric = HealthMetric(
104                name="cpu_health",
105                value=cpu_metrics['usage'],

107                status=status,
108                timestamp=datetime.now(),

110            )

115        except Exception as e:
