117            return self._create_unknown_health_metric("cpu_health")
118
119    async def check_system_health(self) -> Dict:
120        """Check overall system health"""
121        try:
122            health_checks = await asyncio.gather(
123                self._check_cpu_health(),
124                self._check_memory_health(),
125                self._check_disk_health(),
126                self._check_network_health(),
127                self._check_process_health()
128            )
129            
130            overall_status = self._determine_overall_health(health_checks)
131            
132            # Detect anomalies
133            anomalies = await self.anomaly_detector.detect_anomalies(health_checks)
134            
135            # Make predictions
136            predictions = await self._make_health_predictions()
137            
138            return {
139                'timestamp': datetime.now(),
140                'overall_status': overall_status,
141                'component_health': {
142                    check.name: {
143                        'status': check.status,
144                        'value': check.value,
145                        'threshold': check.threshold,
146                        'trend': check.trend
147                    } for check in health_checks
148                },
149                'anomalies': anomalies,
150                'predictions': predictions
151            }
152
153        except Exception as e:
154            self.logger.error(f"Error checking system health: {str(e)}")
155            return self._create_error_health_report()
156
157    def _determine_overall_health(self, health_checks: List[HealthMetric]) -> HealthStatus:
158        """Determine overall system health status"""
159        status_weights = {
160            HealthStatus.CRITICAL: 4,
161            HealthStatus.WARNING: 2,
162            HealthStatus.DEGRADED: 1,
163            HealthStatus.HEALTHY: 0,
164            HealthStatus.UNKNOWN: 3
165        }
166        
167        max_weight = max(status_weights[check.status] for check in health_checks)
168        
169        for status, weight in status_weights.items():
170            if weight == max_weight:
171                return status
172
173    async def _make_health_predictions(self) -> Dict:
174        """Make predictions about future system health"""
175        predictions = {}
176        
177        for metric_name, model in self.predictive_models.items():
178            try:
179                current_data = self._get_prediction_data(metric_name)
180                prediction = await model.predict(current_data)
181                predictions[metric_name] = prediction
182            except Exception as e:
183                self.logger.error(f"Error making prediction for {metric_name}: {str(e)}")
184                
185        return predictions
186
187    async def get_health_report(self, 
188                              component: Optional[str] = None,
189                              time_range: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict:
190        """Get detailed health report"""
191        try:
192            if component and component in self.monitors:
193                return await self._get_component_health_report(component, time_range)
194            
195            return await self._get_full_health_report(time_range)
196
197        except Exception as e:
198            self.logger.error(f"Error generating health report: {str(e)}")
199            return self._create_error_health_report()
200
201    async def _get_component_health_report(self, 
202                                         component: str,
203                                         time_range: Optional[str]) -> Dict:
204        """Get health report for specific component"""
205        monitor = self.monitors[component]
206        metrics = await monitor.get_health_metrics()
207        history = await self._get_metric_history(component, time_range)
208        
209        return {
210            'component': component,
211            'current_status': self.health_metrics.get(f"{component}_health"),
212            'metrics': metrics,
213            'history': history,
214            'predictions': self.predictive_models.get(component)
215        }
216
217    class AnomalyDetector:
218        """Handles anomaly detection in system metrics"""
219        
220        def __init__(self):
221            self.model = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1)
222            self.training_data = []
223
224        async def detect_anomalies(self, metrics: List[HealthMetric]) -> List[Dict]:
225            """Detect anomalies in current metrics"""
226            try:
227                current_data = self._prepare_data(metrics)
228                predictions = self.model.predict(current_data)
229                
230                anomalies = []
231                for i, pred in enumerate(predictions):
232                    if pred == -1:  # Anomaly detected
233                        anomalies.append({
234                            'metric': metrics[i].name,
235                            'value': metrics[i].value,
236                            'timestamp': metrics[i].timestamp
237                        })
238                
239                return anomalies
240
241            except Exception as e:
242                logging.error(f"Error detecting anomalies: {str(e)}")
243                return []
244
245    async def analyze_trends(self, 
246                           component: Optional[str] = None,
247                           timeframe: str = '1h') -> Dict:
248        """Analyze system health trends"""
249        try:
250            if component:
251                return await self._analyze_component_trend(component, timeframe)
252            
253            trends = {}
254            for comp in self.monitors:
255                trends[comp] = await self._analyze_component_trend(comp, timeframe)
256            
257            return {
258                'overall_trend': self._calculate_overall_trend(trends),
259                'component_trends': trends
260            }
261
262        except Exception as e:
263            self.logger.error(f"Error analyzing trends: {str(e)}")
264            return {'error': str(e)}
265
266    async def get_health_forecast(self, 
267                                timeframe: str = '1h') -> Dict:
268        """Get health forecast for specified timeframe"""
269        try:
270            forecasts = {}
271            for component, model in self.predictive_models.items():
272                forecast = await model.forecast(timeframe)
273                forecasts[component] = forecast
274            
275            return {
276                'timestamp': datetime.now(),
277                'forecasts': forecasts,
278                'confidence_scores': self._calculate_confidence_scores(forecasts)
279            }
280
281        except Exception as e:
282            self.logger.error(f"Error generating health forecast: {str(e)}")
283            return {'error': str(e)}
284
285    async def cleanup(self):
286        """Cleanup health monitor resources"""
287        self.logger.info("Cleaning up SystemHealthMonitor")
288        
289        # Cancel health check tasks
290        for task in self.health_tasks.values():
291            task.cancel()
292            
293        try:
294            await asyncio.gather(*self.health_tasks.values())
295        except asyncio.CancelledError:
296            pass
297        
298        # Cleanup monitors
299        for monitor in self.monitors.values():
300            await monitor.cleanup()

9class TuningParameter(Enum):

29class AutoTuner:

91    async def _continuous_tuning(self):
92        """Continuous system tuning loop"""
93        while True:

98                # Generate tuning recommendations

108            except Exception as e:

112    async def _reactive_tuning(self):

137            # Apply the tuning

163            elif tuning.parameter == TuningParameter.IO_SCHEDULER:

173    async def _monitor_tuning_impact(self, tuning: TuningAction):
174        """Monitor the impact of a tuning action"""

192            # Update learning models

194            
195            # Revert if negative impact
196            if impact < -0.2:  # Significant negative impact
197                await self._revert_tuning(tuning)
198
199        except Exception as e:
200            self.logger.error(f"Error monitoring tuning impact: {str(e)}")
201
202    async def _continuous_learning(self):
203        """Continuous learning loop"""
204        while True:
205            try:
206                # Collect training data
207                training_data = await self._collect_training_data()
208                
209                # Update models
210                await self._update_models(training_data)
211                
212                # Adjust learning parameters
213                self._adjust_learning_parameters()
214                
215                await asyncio.sleep(3600)  # Learn every hour
216
217            except Exception as e:
218                self.logger.error(f"Error in continuous learning: {str(e)}")
219                await asyncio.sleep(3600)
220
221    async def get_tuning_recommendations(self) -> List[TuningAction]:
222        """Get current tuning recommendations"""
223        try:
224            system_state = await self._get_system_state()
225            return await self._generate_tuning_recommendations(system_state)
226        except Exception as e:
227            self.logger.error(f"Error getting recommendations: {str(e)}")
228            return []

230    async def get_tuning_history(self, 
231                               parameter: Optional[TuningParameter] = None) -> List[Dict]:
232        """Get tuning history"""
233        try:
234            history = self.tuning_history
235            if parameter:
236                history = [t for t in history if t.parameter == parameter]
237            
238            return [self._tuning_to_dict(t) for t in history]
239        except Exception as e:

241            return []
242
243    def _tuning_to_dict(self, tuning: TuningAction) -> Dict:
244        """Convert tuning action to dictionary"""
245        return {
246            'parameter': tuning.parameter.value,
247            'current_value': tuning.current_value,
248            'new_value': tuning.new_value,
249            'confidence': tuning.confidence,
250            'impact_score': tuning.impact_score,
251            'timestamp': tuning.timestamp.isoformat(),
252            'reason': tuning.reason
253        }
254
255    async def get_performance_impact(self, 
256                                   parameter: TuningParameter) -> Dict:
257        """Get performance impact of parameter tuning"""
258        try:
259            impact_history = [
260                t for t in self.tuning_history 
261                if t.parameter == parameter
262            ]
263            
264            return {
265                'parameter': parameter.value,
266                'average_impact': np.mean([t.impact_score for t in impact_history]),
267                'confidence': self._calculate_confidence(impact_history),
268                'sample_size': len(impact_history)
269            }
270        except Exception as e:
271            self.logger.error(f"Error getting performance impact: {str(e)}")
272            return {}
273
274    async def cleanup(self):
275        """Cleanup auto-tuner resources"""
276        self.logger.info("Cleaning up AutoTuner")
277        
278        # Cancel tuning tasks
279        for task in self.tuning_tasks.values():
280            task.cancel()
281            
282        try:
283            await asyncio.gather(*self.tuning_tasks.values())
284        except asyncio.CancelledError:
285            pass
286        
287        # Save tuning history
288        await self._save_tuning_history()
289        
290        # Cleanup learning models
291        self.learning_models.clear()

Next is the ProcessManager component, which handles process monitoring, optimization, and lifecycle management specifically for development-related processes:

Python
1import asyncio
2from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
3from dataclasses import dataclass
4from enum import Enum
5import psutil
6import os
7import signal
8from datetime import datetime, timedelta
9
10class ProcessPriority(Enum):
11    CRITICAL = 0
12    HIGH = 1
13    NORMAL = 2
14    LOW = 3
15    BACKGROUND = 4
16
17class ProcessState(Enum):
18    RUNNING = "running"
19    SLEEPING = "sleeping"
20    DISK_SLEEP = "disk_sleep"
21    STOPPED = "stopped"
22    TRACING_STOP = "tracing_stop"
23    ZOMBIE = "zombie"
24    DEAD = "dead"
25    WAKE_KILL = "wake_kill"
26    WAKING = "waking"
27
28@dataclass
29class ProcessInfo:
30    pid: int
31    name: str
32    priority: ProcessPriority
33    state: ProcessState
34    cpu_percent: float
35    memory_percent: float
36    io_counters: Optional[Dict]
37    created_time: datetime
38    command_line: str
39    environment: Dict[str, str]
40    is_managed: bool = False
41
42class ProcessManager:
43    def __init__(self):
44        self.logger = logging.getLogger('ProcessManager')
45        self.managed_processes: Dict[int, ProcessInfo] = {}
46        self.process_groups: Dict[str, Set[int]] = {}
47        self.process_history: Dict[int, List[Dict]] = {}
48        
49        # Process patterns for development tools
50        self.dev_process_patterns = {
51            'editors': ['code', 'sublime_text', 'vim', 'atom'],
52            'languages': ['python', 'node', 'java', 'gcc', 'clang'],
53            'tools': ['git', 'docker', 'npm', 'pip'],
54            'databases': ['mysql', 'postgres', 'mongodb'],
55            'servers': ['nginx', 'apache']
56        }
57        
58        # Process optimization rules
59        self.optimization_rules = self._initialize_optimization_rules()
60
61    async def initialize(self):
62        """Initialize the process manager"""
63        try:
64            self.logger.info("Initializing ProcessManager")
65            
66            # Initial process discovery
67            await self._discover_processes()
68            
69            # Start monitoring tasks
70            self.monitoring_tasks = {
71                'process_monitor': asyncio.create_task(self._monitor_processes()),
72                'optimization': asyncio.create_task(self._optimize_processes()),
73                'cleanup': asyncio.create_task(self._cleanup_dead_processes())
74            }
75
76        except Exception as e:
77            self.logger.error(f"Initialization error: {str(e)}")
78            raise
79
80    def _initialize_optimization_rules(self) -> Dict:
81        """Initialize process optimization rules"""
82        return {
83            'idle_editor': {
84                'condition': lambda p: (
85                    any(ed in p.name for ed in self.dev_process_patterns['editors']) and
86                    p.cpu_percent < 1.0
87                ),
88                'action': lambda p: self._set_process_priority(p.pid, ProcessPriority.LOW)
89            },
90            'active_compilation': {
91                'condition': lambda p: (
92                    any(comp in p.name for comp in ['gcc', 'clang', 'javac']) and
93                    p.cpu_percent > 50
94                ),
95                'action': lambda p: self._set_process_priority(p.pid, ProcessPriority.HIGH)
96            },
97            'background_tools': {
98                'condition': lambda p: (
99                    any(tool in p.name for tool in self.dev_process_patterns['tools']) and
100                    p.state == ProcessState.SLEEPING
101                ),
102                'action': lambda p: self._set_process_priority(p.pid, ProcessPriority.BACKGROUND)
103            }
104        }
105
106    async def _monitor_processes(self):
107        """Monitor processes continuously"""
108        while True:
109            try:
110                for pid in list(self.managed_processes.keys()):
111                    try:
112                        process = psutil.Process(pid)
113                        await self._update_process_info(process)
114                    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
115                        await self._handle_dead_process(pid)
116                
117                # Discover new processes
118                await self._discover_processes()
119                
120                await asyncio.sleep(5)  # Update every 5 seconds
121
122            except Exception as e:
123                self.logger.error(f"Error monitoring processes: {str(e)}")
124                await asyncio.sleep(30)
125
126    async def _optimize_processes(self):
127        """Optimize processes based on rules"""
128        while True:
129            try:
130                for process in self.managed_processes.values():
131                    for rule_name, rule in self.optimization_rules.items():
132                        if rule['condition'](process):
133                            await rule['action'](process)
134                
135                await asyncio.sleep(30)  # Check every 30 seconds
136
137            except Exception as e:
138                self.logger.error(f"Error optimizing processes: {str(e)}")
139                await asyncio.sleep(60)
140
141    async def _discover_processes(self):
142        """Discover development-related processes"""
143        try:
144            for process in psutil.process_iter(['pid', 'name', 'cmdline']):
145                try:
146                    if await self._is_dev_process(process):
147                        await self._add_process(process)
148                except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied):
149                    continue
150
151        except Exception as e:
152            self.logger.error(f"Error discovering processes: {str(e)}")
153
154    async def _is_dev_process(self, process: psutil.Process) -> bool:
155        """Check if process is development-related"""
156        try:
157            name = process.name().lower()
158            cmdline = ' '.join(process.cmdline()).lower()
159            
160            for category, patterns in self.dev_process_patterns.items():
161                if any(pattern in name or pattern in cmdline 
162                      for pattern in patterns):
163                    return True
164            
165            return False
166
167        except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied):
168            return False
169
170    async def _add_process(self, process: psutil.Process):
171        """Add process to managed processes"""
172        try:
173            info = await self._get_process_info(process)
174            self.managed_processes[process.pid] = info
175            
176            # Add to process group
177            group = self._determine_process_group(info)
178            if group:
179                if group not in self.process_groups:
180                    self.process_groups[group] = set()
181                self.process_groups[group].add(process.pid)
182
183        except Exception as e:
184            self.logger.error(f"Error adding process {process.pid}: {str(e)}")
185
186    async def _get_process_info(self, process: psutil.Process) -> ProcessInfo:
187        """Get detailed process information"""
188        try:
189            with process.oneshot():
190                return ProcessInfo(
191                    pid=process.pid,
192                    name=process.name(),
193                    priority=self._get_process_priority(process),
194                    state=ProcessState(process.status()),
195                    cpu_percent=process.cpu_percent(),
196                    memory_percent=process.memory_percent(),
197                    io_counters=process.io_counters()._asdict() 
198                        if hasattr(process, 'io_counters') else None,
199                    created_time=datetime.fromtimestamp(process.create_time()),
200                    command_line=' '.join(process.cmdline()),
201                    environment=process.environ(),
202                    is_managed=True
203                )
204
205        except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied) as e:
206            raise Exception(f"Cannot get process info: {str(e)}")
207
208    async def manage_process(self, pid: int) -> bool:
209        """Start managing a specific process"""
210        try:
211            process = psutil.Process(pid)
212            if await self._is_dev_process(process):
213                await self._add_process(process)
214                return True
215            return False
216
217        except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
218            return False
219
220    async def optimize_process(self, pid: int) -> bool:
221        """Optimize a specific process"""
222        try:
223            if pid in self.managed_processes:
224                process_info = self.managed_processes[pid]
225                
226                # Apply optimization rules
227                for rule in self.optimization_rules.values():
228                    if rule['condition'](process_info):
229                        await rule['action'](process_info)
230                
231                return True
232            return False
233
234        except Exception as e:
235            self.logger.error(f"Error optimizing process {pid}: {str(e)}")
236            return False
237
238    async def get_process_info(self, pid: int) -> Optional[Dict]:
239        """Get information about a specific process"""
240        try:
241            if pid in self.managed_processes:
242                process_info = self.managed_processes[pid]
243                return {
244                    'pid': process_info.pid,
245                    'name': process_info.name,
246                    'priority': process_info.priority.value,
247                    'state': process_info.state.value,
248                    'cpu_percent': process_info.cpu_percent,
249                    'memory_percent': process_info.memory_percent,
250                    'created_time': process_info.created_time.isoformat(),
251                    'is_managed': process_info.is_managed
252                }
253            return None
254
255        except Exception as e:
256            self.logger.error(f"Error getting process info for {pid}: {str(e)}")
257            return None
258
259    async def get_process_groups(self) -> Dict[str, List[Dict]]:
260        """Get information about process groups"""
261        try:
262            groups = {}
263            for group_name, pids in self.process_groups.items():
264                groups[group_name] = [
265                    await self.get_process_info(pid)
266                    for pid in pids
267                    if pid in self.managed_processes
268                ]
269            return groups
270
271        except Exception as e:
272            self.logger.error(f"Error getting process groups: {str(e)}")
273            return {}
274
275    async def cleanup(self):
276        """Cleanup process manager resources"""
277        self.logger.info("Cleaning up ProcessManager")
278        
279        # Cancel monitoring tasks
280        for task in self.monitoring_tasks.values():
281            task.cancel()
282            
283        try:
284            await asyncio.gather(*self.monitoring_tasks.values())
285        except asyncio.CancelledError:
286            pass
287        
288        # Clear process data
289        self.managed_processes.clear()
290        self.process_groups.clear()
291        self.process_history.clear()

1import asyncio
2from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
3from datetime import datetime, timedelta
4import numpy as np
5import pandas as pd
6from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
7from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
8from dataclasses import dataclass
9import joblib
10
11@dataclass
12class PredictionResult:
13    resource_type: str
14    current_value: float
15    predicted_value: float
16    confidence: float
17    timestamp: datetime
18    horizon: timedelta
19    features: Dict[str, float]
20
21class ResourcePredictor:
22    def __init__(self):
23        self.logger = logging.getLogger('ResourcePredictor')
24        
25        # Initialize predictive models
26        self.models = {
27            'cpu': self._create_model(),
28            'memory': self._create_model(),
29            'disk_io': self._create_model(),
30            'network': self._create_model()
31        }
32        
33        # Data preprocessing
34        self.scalers = {
35            'cpu': StandardScaler(),
36            'memory': StandardScaler(),
37            'disk_io': StandardScaler(),
38            'network': StandardScaler()
39        }
40        
41        # Prediction configurations
42        self.prediction_horizons = [
43            timedelta(minutes=5),
44            timedelta(minutes=15),
45            timedelta(minutes=30),
46            timedelta(hours=1)
47        ]
48        
49        # Historical data
50        self.historical_data = {}
51        
52        # Model performance metrics
53        self.model_metrics = {}
54
55    async def initialize(self):
56        """Initialize the resource predictor"""
57        try:
58            self.logger.info("Initializing ResourcePredictor")
59            
60            # Load historical data
61            await self._load_historical_data()
62            
63            # Train initial models
64            await self._train_models()
65            
66            # Start prediction tasks
67            self.prediction_tasks = {
68                'training': asyncio.create_task(self._continuous_training()),
69                'evaluation': asyncio.create_task(self._evaluate_models()),
70                'cleanup': asyncio.create_task(self._cleanup_old_data())
71            }
72
73        except Exception as e:
74            self.logger.error(f"Initialization error: {str(e)}")
75            raise
76
77    def _create_model(self) -> RandomForestRegressor:
78        """Create a new prediction model"""
79        return RandomForestRegressor(
80            n_estimators=100,
81            max_depth=10,
82            random_state=42,
83            n_jobs=-1
84        )
85
86    async def predict_resource_usage(self, 
87                                   resource_type: str,
88                                   horizon: timedelta) -> Optional[PredictionResult]:
89        """Predict future resource usage"""
90        try:
91            # Get current features
92            features = await self._get_current_features(resource_type)
93            
94            # Scale features
95            scaled_features = self.scalers[resource_type].transform([features])
96            
97            # Make prediction
98            model = self.models[resource_type]
99            prediction = model.predict(scaled_features)[0]
100            
101            # Calculate confidence
102            confidence = self._calculate_prediction_confidence(
103                model, scaled_features, resource_type
104            )
105            
106            return PredictionResult(
107                resource_type=resource_type,
108                current_value=features['current_value'],
109                predicted_value=prediction,
110                confidence=confidence,
111                timestamp=datetime.now(),
112                horizon=horizon,
113                features=features
114            )
115
116        except Exception as e:
117            self.logger.error(f"Error predicting {resource_type} usage: {str(e)}")
118            return None
119
120    async def _get_current_features(self, resource_type: str) -> Dict[str, float]:
121        """Get current feature values for prediction"""
122        try:
123            # Get basic metrics
124            metrics = await self._get_system_metrics()
125            
126            # Calculate derived features
127            time_features = self._get_time_features()
128            trend_features = await self._calculate_trend_features(resource_type)
129            
130            return {
131                'current_value': metrics[resource_type],
132                'hour_of_day': time_features['hour'],
133                'day_of_week': time_features['day'],
134                'trend_1h': trend_features['1h'],
135                'trend_4h': trend_features['4h'],
136                'load_average': metrics['load_average'],
137                'process_count': metrics['process_count']
138            }
139
140        except Exception as e:
141            self.logger.error(f"Error getting features: {str(e)}")
142            raise
143
144    async def _continuous_training(self):
145        """Continuous model training loop"""
146        while True:
147            try:
148                # Check if retraining is needed
149                if await self._should_retrain():
150                    # Get training data
151                    training_data = await self._prepare_training_data()
152                    
153                    # Train models
154                    for resource_type, model in self.models.items():
155                        X, y = self._prepare_resource_training_data(
156                            training_data, resource_type
157                        )
158                        
159                        # Scale features
160                        X_scaled = self.scalers[resource_type].fit_transform(X)
161                        
162                        # Train model
163                        model.fit(X_scaled, y)
164                        
165                        # Update metrics
166                        self._update_model_metrics(resource_type, X_scaled, y)
167                
168                await asyncio.sleep(3600)  # Train every hour
169
170            except Exception as e:
171                self.logger.error(f"Error in continuous training: {str(e)}")
172                await asyncio.sleep(3600)
173
174    async def _evaluate_models(self):
175        """Evaluate model performance"""
176        while True:
177            try:
178                for resource_type, model in self.models.items():
179                    # Get evaluation data
180                    eval_data = await self._get_evaluation_data(resource_type)
181                    
182                    # Evaluate model
183                    metrics = await self._evaluate_model(
184                        model, 
185                        eval_data, 
186                        resource_type
187                    )
188                    
189                    # Update metrics
190                    self.model_metrics[resource_type] = metrics
191                    
192                    # Log performance
193                    self._log_model_performance(resource_type, metrics)
194                
195                await asyncio.sleep(1800)  # Evaluate every 30 minutes
196
197            except Exception as e:
198                self.logger.error(f"Error evaluating models: {str(e)}")
199                await asyncio.sleep(1800)
200
201    async def _evaluate_model(self, 
202                            model: RandomForestRegressor,
203                            eval_data: Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray],
204                            resource_type: str) -> Dict:
205        """Evaluate model performance"""
206        X_eval, y_eval = eval_data
207        
208        # Scale features
209        X_scaled = self.scalers[resource_type].transform(X_eval)
210        
211        # Make predictions
212        predictions = model.predict(X_scaled)
213        
214        # Calculate metrics
215        mse = np.mean((predictions - y_eval) ** 2)
216        mae = np.mean(np.abs(predictions - y_eval))
217        r2 = model.score(X_scaled, y_eval)
218        
219        return {
220            'mse': mse,
221            'mae': mae,
222            'r2': r2,
223            'timestamp': datetime.now()
224        }
225
226    def _calculate_prediction_confidence(self,
227                                      model: RandomForestRegressor,
228                                      features: np.ndarray,
229                                      resource_type: str) -> float:
230        """Calculate confidence score for prediction"""
231        try:
232            # Get predictions from all trees
233            predictions = np.array([
234                tree.predict(features)
235                for tree in model.estimators_
236            ])
237            
238            # Calculate standard deviation of predictions
239            std = np.std(predictions)
240            
241            # Calculate confidence based on standard deviation
242            confidence = 1.0 / (1.0 + std)
243            
244            # Adjust confidence based on model performance
245            if resource_type in self.model_metrics:
246                r2 = self.model_metrics[resource_type]['r2']
247                confidence *= r2
248            
249            return min(max(confidence, 0.0), 1.0)
250
251        except Exception as e:
252            self.logger.error(f"Error calculating confidence: {str(e)}")
253            return 0.0
254
255    async def get_predictions(self, 
256                            resource_types: Optional[List[str]] = None,
257                            horizon: Optional[timedelta] = None) -> Dict[str, PredictionResult]:
258        """Get predictions for specified resources"""
259        try:
260            if resource_types is None:
261                resource_types = list(self.models.keys())
262            
263            if horizon is None:
264                horizon = self.prediction_horizons[0]
265            
266            predictions = {}
267            for resource_type in resource_types:
268                prediction = await self.predict_resource_usage(
269                    resource_type, horizon
270                )
271                if prediction:
272                    predictions[resource_type] = prediction
273            
274            return predictions
275
276        except Exception as e:
277            self.logger.error(f"Error getting predictions: {str(e)}")
278            return {}
279
280    async def get_model_metrics(self) -> Dict[str, Dict]:
281        """Get model performance metrics"""
282        return self.model_metrics
283
284    async def cleanup(self):
285        """Cleanup predictor resources"""
286        self.logger.info("Cleaning up ResourcePredictor")
287        
288        # Cancel prediction tasks
289        for task in self.prediction_tasks.values():
290            task.cancel()
291            
292        try:
293            await asyncio.gather(*self.prediction_tasks.values())
294        except asyncio.CancelledError:
295            pass
296        
297        # Save models and data
298        await self._save_models()
299        await self._save_historical_data()

Let's move on to the next component, which is the WorkloadOptimizer. This component focuses on optimizing system workloads based on usage patterns and resource predictions:

Python
1import asyncio
2from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
3from dataclasses import dataclass
4from enum import Enum
5from datetime import datetime, timedelta
6import numpy as np
7
8class WorkloadType(Enum):
9    DEVELOPMENT = "development"
10    BUILD = "build"
11    TEST = "test"
12    DATABASE = "database"
13    NETWORK = "network"
14    BACKGROUND = "background"
15
16class OptimizationStrategy(Enum):
17    AGGRESSIVE = "aggressive"
18    BALANCED = "balanced"
19    CONSERVATIVE = "conservative"
20    ADAPTIVE = "adaptive"
21
22@dataclass
23class WorkloadProfile:
24    type: WorkloadType
25    processes: Set[int]
26    resource_usage: Dict[str, float]
27    priority: int
28    start_time: datetime
29    duration: Optional[timedelta] = None
30    dependencies: Set[str] = None
31
32@dataclass
33class OptimizationPlan:
34    workload_id: str
35    actions: List[Dict]
36    expected_impact: float
37    priority: int
38    timestamp: datetime
39    strategy: OptimizationStrategy
40
41class WorkloadOptimizer:
42    def __init__(self):
43        self.logger = logging.getLogger('WorkloadOptimizer')
44        self.active_workloads: Dict[str, WorkloadProfile] = {}
45        self.optimization_history: List[Dict] = []
46        self.current_strategy = OptimizationStrategy.BALANCED
47        
48        # Optimization thresholds
49        self.thresholds = {
50            'cpu_high': 80.0,
51            'memory_high': 85.0,
52            'io_high': 70.0,
53            'network_high': 75.0
54        }
55        
56        # Strategy configurations
57        self.strategy_configs = self._initialize_strategy_configs()
58
59    async def initialize(self):
60        """Initialize the workload optimizer"""
61        try:
62            self.logger.info("Initializing WorkloadOptimizer")
63            
64            # Load optimization history
65            await self._load_optimization_history()
66            
67            # Start optimization tasks
68            self.optimization_tasks = {
69                'monitor': asyncio.create_task(self._monitor_workloads()),
70                'optimize': asyncio.create_task(self._optimize_workloads()),
71                'evaluate': asyncio.create_task(self._evaluate_optimizations())
72            }
73
74        except Exception as e:
75            self.logger.error(f"Initialization error: {str(e)}")
76            raise
77
78    def _initialize_strategy_configs(self) -> Dict:
79        """Initialize optimization strategy configurations"""
80        return {
81            OptimizationStrategy.AGGRESSIVE: {
82                'cpu_threshold': 70.0,
83                'memory_threshold': 75.0,
84                'io_threshold': 60.0,
85                'priority_boost': 2,
86                'resource_limit_multiplier': 0.8
87            },
88            OptimizationStrategy.BALANCED: {
89                'cpu_threshold': 80.0,
90                'memory_threshold': 85.0,
91                'io_threshold': 70.0,
92                'priority_boost': 1,
93                'resource_limit_multiplier': 1.0
94            },
95            OptimizationStrategy.CONSERVATIVE: {
96                'cpu_threshold': 90.0,
97                'memory_threshold': 90.0,
98                'io_threshold': 80.0,
99                'priority_boost': 0,
100                'resource_limit_multiplier': 1.2
101            }
102        }
103
104    async def register_workload(self, 
105                              workload_type: WorkloadType,
106                              processes: Set[int],
107                              priority: int = 1) -> str:
108        """Register a new workload for optimization"""
109        try:
110            workload_id = self._generate_workload_id()
111            
112            profile = WorkloadProfile(
113                type=workload_type,
114                processes=processes,
115                resource_usage=await self._get_resource_usage(processes),
116                priority=priority,
117                start_time=datetime.now()
118            )
119            
120            self.active_workloads[workload_id] = profile
121            
122            # Initial optimization
123            await self._optimize_workload(workload_id)
124            
125            return workload_id
126
127        except Exception as e:
128            self.logger.error(f"Error registering workload: {str(e)}")
129            raise
130
131    async def _monitor_workloads(self):
132        """Monitor active workloads"""
133        while True:
134            try:
135                for workload_id, profile in list(self.active_workloads.items()):
136                    # Update resource usage
137                    profile.resource_usage = await self._get_resource_usage(
138                        profile.processes
139                    )
140                    
141                    # Check for completed workloads
142                    if await self._is_workload_completed(workload_id):
143                        await self._cleanup_workload(workload_id)
144                
145                await asyncio.sleep(10)  # Monitor every 10 seconds
146
147            except Exception as e:
148                self.logger.error(f"Error monitoring workloads: {str(e)}")
149                await asyncio.sleep(30)
150
151    async def _optimize_workloads(self):
152        """Optimize active workloads"""
153        while True:
154            try:
155                # Update optimization strategy
156                await self._update_optimization_strategy()
157                
158                for workload_id in list(self.active_workloads.keys()):
159                    await self._optimize_workload(workload_id)
160                
161                await asyncio.sleep(30)  # Optimize every 30 seconds
162
163            except Exception as e:
164                self.logger.error(f"Error optimizing workloads: {str(e)}")
165                await asyncio.sleep(60)
166
167    async def _optimize_workload(self, workload_id: str) -> Optional[OptimizationPlan]:
168        """Optimize a specific workload"""
169        try:
170            profile = self.active_workloads.get(workload_id)
171            if not profile:
172                return None
173
174            # Generate optimization plan
175            plan = await self._generate_optimization_plan(profile)
176            
177            if plan:
178                # Apply optimization actions
179                success = await self._apply_optimization_plan(plan)
180                
181                if success:
182                    # Record optimization
183                    await self._record_optimization(plan)
184                    return plan
185
186            return None
187
188        except Exception as e:
189            self.logger.error(f"Error optimizing workload {workload_id}: {str(e)}")
190            return None
191
192    async def _generate_optimization_plan(self, 
193                                       profile: WorkloadProfile) -> Optional[OptimizationPlan]:
194        """Generate optimization plan for workload"""
195        try:
196            actions = []
197            strategy_config = self.strategy_configs[self.current_strategy]
198            
199            # CPU optimization
200            if profile.resource_usage['cpu'] > strategy_config['cpu_threshold']:
201                actions.append({
202                    'type': 'cpu',
203                    'action': 'adjust_priority',
204                    'params': {
205                        'priority_adjustment': strategy_config['priority_boost']
206                    }
207                })
208
209            # Memory optimization
210            if profile.resource_usage['memory'] > strategy_config['memory_threshold']:
211                actions.append({
212                    'type': 'memory',
213                    'action': 'limit_memory',
214                    'params': {
215                        'limit_multiplier': strategy_config['resource_limit_multiplier']
216                    }
217                })
218
219            # I/O optimization
220            if profile.resource_usage['io'] > strategy_config['io_threshold']:
221                actions.append({
222                    'type': 'io',
223                    'action': 'optimize_io',
224                    'params': {
225                        'io_priority': 'idle'
226                    }
227                })
228
229            if actions:
230                return OptimizationPlan(
231                    workload_id=self._generate_workload_id(),
232                    actions=actions,
233                    expected_impact=self._calculate_expected_impact(actions),
234                    priority=profile.priority,
235                    timestamp=datetime.now(),
236                    strategy=self.current_strategy
237                )
238
239            return None
240
241        except Exception as e:
242            self.logger.error(f"Error generating optimization plan: {str(e)}")
243            return None
244
245    async def _apply_optimization_plan(self, plan: OptimizationPlan) -> bool:
246        """Apply optimization plan"""
247        try:
248            success = True
249            for action in plan.actions:
250                if not await self._apply_optimization_action(action):
251                    success = False
252            
253            return success
254
255        except Exception as e:
256            self.logger.error(f"Error applying optimization plan: {str(e)}")
257            return False
258
259    async def get_workload_status(self, workload_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
260        """Get current status of a workload"""
261        try:
262            if workload_id in self.active_workloads:
263                profile = self.active_workloads[workload_id]
264                return {
265                    'workload_id': workload_id,
266                    'type': profile.type.value,
267                    'resource_usage': profile.resource_usage,
268                    'priority': profile.priority,
269                    'start_time': profile.start_time.isoformat(),
270                    'duration': str(profile.duration) if profile.duration else None,
271                    'process_count': len(profile.processes)
272                }
273            return None
274
275        except Exception as e:
276            self.logger.error(f"Error getting workload status: {str(e)}")
277            return None
278
279    async def cleanup(self):
280        """Cleanup optimizer resources"""
281        self.logger.info("Cleaning up WorkloadOptimizer")
282        
283        # Cancel optimization tasks
284        for task in self.optimization_tasks.values():
285            task.cancel()
286            
287        try:
288            await asyncio.gather(*self.optimization_tasks.values())
289        except asyncio.CancelledError:
290            pass
291        
292        # Cleanup active workloads
293        for workload_id in list(self.active_workloads.keys()):
294            await self._cleanup_workload(workload_id)

3import asyncio
4from typing import Dict, Optional
5import logging
6from datetime import datetime
7from dataclasses import dataclass
8from enum import Enum
9
10class SystemState(Enum):
11    INITIALIZING = "initializing"
12    RUNNING = "running"
13    OPTIMIZING = "optimizing"
14    PAUSED = "paused"
15    ERROR = "error"
16    STOPPED = "stopped"
17
18@dataclass
19class OptimizationResult:
20    timestamp: datetime
21    success: bool
22    actions_taken: List[str]

25
26class SystemOptimizer:
27    def __init__(self):
28        # Setup logging
29        self.logger = logging.getLogger('SystemOptimizer')
30        self.logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
31        
32        # System state
33        self.state = SystemState.INITIALIZING
34        self.last_optimization: Optional[OptimizationResult] = None
35        
36        # Performance tracking
37        self.performance_metrics = {
38            'optimizations_performed': 0,
39            'successful_optimizations': 0,
40            'failed_optimizations': 0,
41            'total_runtime': 0
42        }
43        
44        # Component tracking
45        self.components = {}
46        self.start_time = None
47
48    async def initialize(self):
49        """Initialize the system optimizer and its components"""
50        try:
51            self.logger.info("Initializing SystemOptimizer")
52            
53            # Initialize core components
54            self.components = {
55                'resource_monitor': ResourceMonitor(),
56                'health_monitor': SystemHealthMonitor(),
57                'pattern_analyzer': PatternAnalyzer(),
58                'auto_tuner': AutoTuner(),
59                'process_manager': ProcessManager(),
60                'metrics_collector': MetricsCollector()
61            }
62            
63            # Initialize each component
64            for name, component in self.components.items():
65                try:
66                    self.logger.info(f"Initializing {name}")
67                    await component.initialize()
68                    self.logger.info(f"{name} initialized successfully")
69                except Exception as e:
70                    self.logger.error(f"Failed to initialize {name}: {str(e)}")
71                    self.state = SystemState.ERROR
72                    raise
73
74            self.state = SystemState.RUNNING
75            self.start_time = datetime.now()
76            self.logger.info("SystemOptimizer initialization complete")
77
78        except Exception as e:
79            self.logger.error(f"SystemOptimizer initialization failed: {str(e)}")
80            self.state = SystemState.ERROR
81            raise
82
83    async def start_optimization(self):
84        """Start the optimization process"""
85        if self.state != SystemState.RUNNING:
86            raise RuntimeError(f"Cannot start optimization in state: {self.state}")
87
88        try:
89            self.logger.info("Starting optimization process")
90            self.state = SystemState.OPTIMIZING
91            
92            # Start continuous monitoring and optimization
93            self.optimization_task = asyncio.create_task(self._optimization_loop())
94            self.monitoring_task = asyncio.create_task(self._monitoring_loop())
95            
96            # Start health monitoring
97            self.health_task = asyncio.create_task(self._health_monitoring_loop())
98
99        except Exception as e:
100            self.logger.error(f"Failed to start optimization: {str(e)}")
101            self.state = SystemState.ERROR
102            raise
103
104    async def _optimization_loop(self):
105        """Main optimization loop"""
106        while self.state == SystemState.OPTIMIZING:
107            try:
108                # Get current system state
109                system_metrics = await self.components['metrics_collector'].get_metrics()
110                
111                # Check system health
112                health_status = await self.components['health_monitor'].check_health()
113                
114                # Analyze patterns
115                patterns = await self.components['pattern_analyzer'].analyze_metrics(system_metrics)
116                
117                # Determine if optimization is needed
118                if await self._should_optimize(health_status, patterns):
119                    optimization_result = await self._perform_optimization(
120                        system_metrics, 
121                        health_status, 
122                        patterns
123                    )
124                    await self._handle_optimization_result(optimization_result)
125                
126                await asyncio.sleep(5)  # Adjust based on system needs
127
128            except Exception as e:
129                self.logger.error(f"Error in optimization loop: {str(e)}")
130                await asyncio.sleep(30)  # Back off on error
131
132    async def _monitoring_loop(self):
133        """Continuous system monitoring loop"""
134        while self.state in [SystemState.RUNNING, SystemState.OPTIMIZING]:
135            try:
136                # Collect system metrics
137                metrics = await self.components['resource_monitor'].collect_metrics()
138                
139                # Store metrics
140                await self.components['metrics_collector'].store_metrics(metrics)
141                
142                # Update process information
143                await self.components['process_manager'].update_processes()
144                
145                await asyncio.sleep(1)  # High-frequency monitoring
146
147            except Exception as e:
148                self.logger.error(f"Error in monitoring loop: {str(e)}")
149                await asyncio.sleep(5)
150
151    async def _health_monitoring_loop(self):
152        """System health monitoring loop"""
153        while self.state in [SystemState.RUNNING, SystemState.OPTIMIZING]:
154            try:
155                health_status = await self.components['health_monitor'].check_health()
156                
157                if health_status.is_critical:
158                    await self._handle_critical_health(health_status)
159                
160                await asyncio.sleep(10)  # Health check interval
161
162            except Exception as e:
163                self.logger.error(f"Error in health monitoring: {str(e)}")
164                await asyncio.sleep(30)
165
166    async def _should_optimize(self, health_status, patterns) -> bool:
167        """Determine if optimization should be performed"""
168        if health_status.is_critical:
169            return True
170            
171        if health_status.needs_optimization:
172            return True
173            
174        if any(p.requires_optimization for p in patterns):
175            return True
176            
177        return False

179    async def _perform_optimization(self, 
180                                  metrics: Dict, 
181                                  health_status: Dict, 
182                                  patterns: List) -> OptimizationResult:
183        """Perform system optimization"""

189                metrics,

192            )
193            
194            actions_taken = []

197            # Apply optimizations

199                success = await self.components['auto_tuner'].apply_optimization(rec)
200                if success:
201                    actions_taken.append(rec.action_type)
202                    resource_impacts.update(rec.expected_impact)

204            return OptimizationResult(
205                timestamp=datetime.now(),
206                success=bool(actions_taken),
207                actions_taken=actions_taken,
208                resource_impacts=resource_impacts
209            )
210
211        except Exception as e:
212            self.logger.error(f"Optimization failed: {str(e)}")
213            return OptimizationResult(

215                success=False,
216                actions_taken=[],

236        self.state = SystemState.STOPPED

256            'last_optimization': self.last_optimization,

123        if not self.current_state:

139            if time_since_last < 60:  # Minimum 1 minute between optimizations

151        
152        return False

47async def _run_optimization_loop(self):
48    """Core optimization loop"""
49    while self.is_running:
50        try:

52            metrics = await self.monitor.collect_metrics()
53            self.current_state = SystemMetrics(**metrics)

67            await asyncio.sleep(sleep_time)

71            await asyncio.sleep(5)  # Basic error backoff

73async def _handle_optimizations(self, optimizations: List[Dict]):
74    """Handle optimization recommendations"""
75    for opt in optimizations:
76        priority = opt.get('priority', 'medium')
77        await self.optimization_queue.put({
78            'type': opt['type'],
79            'params': opt['params'],
80            'priority': priority
81        })

104        elif self.current_state.cpu_usage < 20:
105            return base_interval / 2

import json
import yaml
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
from pathlib import Path
import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from watchdog.observers import Observer
from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler

@dataclass
class SystemConfig:
sampling_rate: int = 5
history_size: int = 1000
log_level: str = "INFO"
max_cpu_usage: float = 80.0
max_memory_usage: float = 85.0
optimization_threshold: float = 0.8
backup_enabled: bool = True
auto_tune: bool = True

@dataclass
class UserPreferences:
priority_processes: list = None
ignored_processes: list = None
quiet_hours: Dict[str, str] = None
optimization_aggressiveness: float = 0.5
notification_level: str = "IMPORTANT"

class ConfigManager:
def init(self, config_path: str = "config"):
self.logger = logging.getLogger('ConfigManager')
self.config_path = Path(config_path)
self.config_file = self.config_path / "system_config.yaml"
self.preferences_file = self.config_path / "user_preferences.yaml"

1    # Initialize configurations
2    self.system_config = SystemConfig()
3    self.user_preferences = UserPreferences()
4    
5    # Configuration locks
6    self.config_lock = asyncio.Lock()
7    
8    # Change tracking
9    self.pending_changes: Dict[str, Any] = {}
10    self.last_modified = {}
11    
12    # Setup file watching
13    self.observer = Observer()
14    self.setup_file_watching()
15
16async def initialize(self):
17    """Initialize configuration manager"""
18    try:
19        self.logger.info("Initializing ConfigManager")
20        
21        # Create config directory if it doesn't exist
22        self.config_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
23        
24        # Load configurations
25        await self.load_configurations()
26        
27        # Start file watching
28        self.start_file_watching()
29        
30        # Initialize adaptive config
31        await self.initialize_adaptive_config()
32        
33    except Exception as e:
34        self.logger.error(f"Configuration initialization error: {str(e)}")
35        raise
36
37async def load_configurations(self):
38    """Load all configurations"""
39    async with self.config_lock:
40        try:
41            # Load system configuration
42            if self.config_file.exists():
43                with open(self.config_file) as f:
44                    system_config = yaml.safe_load(f)
45                    self.system_config = SystemConfig(**system_config)
46            else:
47                await self.save_system_config()
48
49            # Load user preferences
50            if self.preferences_file.exists():
51                with open(self.preferences_file) as f:
52                    user_prefs = yaml.safe_load(f)
53                    self.user_preferences = UserPreferences(**user_prefs)
54            else:
55                await self.save_user_preferences()
56
57        except Exception as e:
58            self.logger.error(f"Error loading configurations: {str(e)}")
59            raise
60
61async def save_system_config(self):
62    """Save system configuration"""
63    async with self.config_lock:
64        try:
65            with open(self.config_file, 'w') as f:
66                yaml.safe_dump(asdict(self.system_config), f)
67            self.last_modified['system_config'] = datetime.now()
68        except Exception as e:
69            self.logger.error(f"Error saving system config: {str(e)}")
70            raise
71
72async def save_user_preferences(self):
73    """Save user preferences"""
74    async with self.config_lock:
75        try:
76            with open(self.preferences_file, 'w') as f:
77                yaml.safe_dump(asdict(self.user_preferences), f)
78            self.last_modified['user_preferences'] = datetime.now()
79        except Exception as e:
80            self.logger.error(f"Error saving user preferences: {str(e)}")
81            raise
82
83def setup_file_watching(self):
84    """Setup file system watching for config files"""
85    class ConfigFileHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
86        def __init__(self, config_manager):
87            self.config_manager = config_manager
88
89        def on_modified(self, event):
90            if not event.is_directory:
91                if event.src_path.endswith('system_config.yaml'):
92                    asyncio.create_task(
93                        self.config_manager.handle_config_change('system_config')
94                    )
95                elif event.src_path.endswith('user_preferences.yaml'):
96                    asyncio.create_task(
97                        self.config_manager.handle_config_change('user_preferences')
98                    )
99
100    self.observer.schedule(
101        ConfigFileHandler(self),
102        str(self.config_path),
103        recursive=False
104    )
105
106def start_file_watching(self):
107    """Start file system observer"""
108    self.observer.start()
109
110async def handle_config_change(self, config_type: str):
111    """Handle configuration file changes"""
112    try:
113        async with self.config_lock:
114            if config_type == 'system_config':
115                await self.load_configurations()
116                await self.apply_system_config_changes()
117            elif config_type == 'user_preferences':
118                await self.load_configurations()
119                await self.apply_user_preference_changes()
120            
121            # Notify subscribers
122            await self.notify_config_changes(config_type)
123            
124    except Exception as e:
125        self.logger.error(f"Error handling config change: {str(e)}")
126
127async def apply_system_config_changes(self):
128    """Apply changes in system configuration"""
129    try:
130        # Apply sampling rate changes
131        if 'sampling_rate' in self.pending_changes:
132            await self.update_sampling_rate(
133                self.pending_changes['sampling_rate']
134            )
135        
136        # Apply other system changes
137        for key, value in self.pending_changes.items():
138            if hasattr(self.system_config, key):
139                setattr(self.system_config, key, value)
140        
141        self.pending_changes.clear()
142        
143    except Exception as e:
144        self.logger.error(f"Error applying system config changes: {str(e)}")
145        raise
146
147async def initialize_adaptive_config(self):
148    """Initialize adaptive configuration system"""
149    self.adaptive_config = {
150        'performance_metrics': {},
151        'optimization_history': [],
152        'system_patterns': {},
153        'adaptation_rules': self._load_adaptation_rules()
154    }
155
156def _load_adaptation_rules(self) -> Dict:
157    """Load adaptation rules for adaptive configuration"""
158    return {
159        'cpu_intensive': {
160            'condition': lambda metrics: metrics['cpu_usage'] > 75,
161            'actions': [
162                ('sampling_rate', 'increase'),
163                ('optimization_threshold', 'decrease')
164            ]
165        },
166        'memory_intensive': {

168            'actions': [
169                ('optimization_threshold', 'decrease'),
170                ('backup_enabled', False)
171            ]
172        }
173    }
174
175async def update_adaptive_config(self, metrics: Dict):
176    """Update adaptive configuration based on system metrics"""
177    try:
178        for rule_name, rule in self.adaptive_config['adaptation_rules'].items():
179            if rule['condition'](metrics):
180                await self._apply_adaptation_rule(rule['actions'])
181    except Exception as e:
182        self.logger.error(f"Error updating adaptive config: {str(e)}")
183
184async def _apply_adaptation_rule(self, actions: list):
185    """Apply adaptation rule actions"""
186    async with self.config_lock:
187        for param, action in actions:
188            if hasattr(self.system_config, param):
189                current_value = getattr(self.system_config, param)
190                new_value = self._calculate_adapted_value(
191                    param, current_value, action
192                )
193                setattr(self.system_config, param, new_value)
194

197def _calculate_adapted_value(self, param: str, current_value: Any, action: str) -> Any:
198    """Calculate new value based on adaptation action"""
199    if isinstance(current_value, (int, float)):

201            return current_value * 1.2
202        elif action == 'decrease':
203            return current_value * 0.8
204    elif isinstance(current_value, bool):
205        return action if isinstance(action, bool) else current_value
206    return current_value

Claude 3.5 Sonnet

Great question! Let me clarify the relationship between these files:

  1. The YAML files (config.yaml, system_config.yaml, user_preferences.yaml) are configuration DATA files. They store settings and preferences in a human-readable format.

  2. The Python files (system_config.py, user_preferences.py) are the CODE that HANDLES these configurations. They define the data structures (using dataclasses) and the logic for managing the configurations.

So, typically the structure works like this:

Python
1# In config_manager.py
2@dataclass
3class SystemConfig:
4    sampling_rate: int = 5
5    history_size: int = 1000
6    # ... other fields ...
7
8class ConfigManager:
9    def __init__(self):
10        # Load the YAML file
11        with open('config/system_config.yaml') as f:
12            config_data = yaml.safe_load(f)
13            # Convert YAML data into SystemConfig object
14            self.system_config = SystemConfig(**config_data['system_config'])

You could either:

  1. Keep one master config.yaml that contains everything:
YAML
1# config.yaml
2system_config:
3  sampling_rate: 5
4  history_size: 1000
5  # ... other system settings ...
6
7user_preferences:
8  priority_processes: 
9    - "python"
10    - "code"
11  # ... other user preferences ...
  1. Or split into separate files for better organization:
YAML
1# system_config.yaml
2system_config:
3  sampling_rate: 5
4  history_size: 1000
5  # ... other system settings ...
6
7# user_preferences.yaml
8user_preferences:
9  priority_processes: 
10    - "python"
11    - "code"
12  # ... other user preferences ...

I recommend option 2 (separate files) because:

  • Better organization
  • Easier to manage
  • Clearer separation of concerns
  • Easier to update individual components

So:

  1. Keep the Python files (they're the code that manages the config)
  2. Keep the YAML files (they're the actual configuration data)
  3. You can delete the original config.yaml if you're using the split files approach

side note...how do i unmerge a merge that created a divergent branch?

Claude 3.5 Sonnet

To unmerge a merge that created a divergent branch, you have a few options:

  1. If the merge was your last commit:
BASH
1# Reset to the commit before the merge
2git reset --hard HEAD~1
  1. If you know the specific commit hash before the merge:
BASH
1# Reset to a specific commit
2git reset --hard <commit-hash>
  1. To find the merge commit and then undo it:
BASH
1# See the commit history with merge information
2git log --merges
3
4# Then reset to before the merge
5git reset --hard <commit-hash-before-merge>
  1. If you want to keep your changes but undo the merge:
BASH
1# Soft reset (keeps changes in staging)
2git reset --soft HEAD~1
  1. If you've already pushed the merge:
BASH
1# Reset locally
2git reset --hard HEAD~1
3
4# Force push (be careful with this!)
5git push --force origin <branch-name>

To check your branch status first:

BASH
1# See branch structure
2git log --graph --oneline --all
3
4# See current branch status
5git status
6
7# See branch divergence point
8git merge-base <branch1> <branch2>

CAUTION:

  • --hard resets will delete changes permanently
  • --force pushes can affect other developers
  • Always make sure you have a backup or know what you're resetting to

Would you like me to explain any of these approaches in more detail?

how do i change default branch and delete a branch

Claude 3.5 Sonnet

Here's how to change the default branch and delete a branch:

Change Default Branch:

BASH
1# Locally
2git branch -m old_branch new_branch
3
4# On GitHub:
51. Go to repository Settings
62. Click Branches in left sidebar
73. Click pencil icon next to default branch
84. Select new default branch
95. Click Update
10
11# Or via command line for GitHub:
12git push -u origin new_branch
13git push origin --delete old_branch

Delete a Branch:

BASH
1# Delete branch locally
2git branch -d branch_name     # Safe delete (won't delete if not merged)
3git branch -D branch_name     # Force delete
4
5# Delete branch remotely (on GitHub)
6git push origin --delete branch_name
7# or
8git push origin :branch_name

Complete Process Example:

BASH
1# Change from 'master' to 'main'
2git branch -m master main           # Rename locally
3git push -u origin main            # Push new branch to remote
4git push origin --delete master    # Delete old branch from remote
5
6# Delete an unwanted branch
7git branch -D unwanted_branch      # Delete locally
8git push origin --delete unwanted_branch  # Delete from remote

ok...i've ran the setup script and i'm looking updating the .env file. But how do i set up a new user for my database and how do i create a secret key?

Claude 3.5 Sonnet

Here's how to set up both:

Generate a Django Secret Key:

BASH
1# Run Python in terminal
2python -c "from django.core.management.utils import get_random_secret_key; print(get_random_secret_key())"

This will output a random secret key you can copy into your .env file.

For PostgreSQL User Setup:

BASH
1# Log into PostgreSQL as postgres user
2sudo -u postgres psql
3
4# Create a new user (replace 'youruser' and 'yourpassword')
5CREATE USER youruser WITH PASSWORD 'yourpassword';
6
7# Create database
8CREATE DATABASE system_optimizer;
9
10# Grant privileges to your user
11ALTER USER youruser CREATEDB;
12GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE system_optimizer TO youruser;
13
14# Make your user the owner of the database
15ALTER DATABASE system_optimizer OWNER TO youruser;
16
17# Exit PostgreSQL
18\q

Then update your .env file:

BASH
1DJANGO_SECRET_KEY='your-generated-secret-key'
2DEBUG=True
3DB_NAME=system_optimizer
4DB_USER=youruser
5DB_PASSWORD=yourpassword
6DB_HOST=localhost
7DB_PORT=5432

Complete step-by-step:

BASH
1# 1. Generate secret key
2python -c "from django.core.management.utils import get_random_secret_key; print(get_random_secret_key())"
3
4# 2. Create PostgreSQL user and database
5sudo -u postgres psql
6
7# In PostgreSQL prompt:
8CREATE USER youruser WITH PASSWORD 'yourpassword';
9CREATE DATABASE system_optimizer;
10ALTER USER youruser CREATEDB;
11GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE system_optimizer TO youruser;
12ALTER DATABASE system_optimizer OWNER TO youruser;
13\q
14
15# 3. Test connection
16psql -U youruser -d system_optimizer -h localhost
17
18# 4. Update .env file with the new credentials

can i tell it not use a # in the code? it's automatically commenting out the section of the key that follows the # sign

Claude 3.5 Sonnet

Yes! The Django secret key can contain any characters except the # since it's causing issues in the .env file. Let's generate a key without #:

BASH
1# Method 1: Using Python to generate a key without #
2python -c "import secrets; print(''.join(c for c in secrets.token_urlsafe(50) if c != '#'))"
3
4# Method 2: Using OpenSSL (alternative method)
5openssl rand -base64 50 | tr -d '#'

Then in your .env file:

1DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=your_generated_key_without_hashtag
2DEBUG=True
3DB_NAME=system_optimizer
4DB_USER=youruser
5DB_PASSWORD=yourpassword
6DB_HOST=localhost
7DB_PORT=5432

Or you can wrap the key in quotes in your .env file:

1DJANGO_SECRET_KEY="your_generated_key_with_any_characters_including_#"

what is LC_ALL? it's the part that kept throwing errors...it makes me a little bit anxious to be trying to set something that was throwing errors before...i'll just be out here, eyes squeezed shut, holding my breath and pressing the enter key with one finger and making a face like the whole thing is about to explode...don't mind me. hahaha

Claude 3.5 Sonnet

Haha! I love that description - we've all had those "please don't explode" moments with Linux!

LC_ALL is basically the "nuclear option" of locale settings. It's a way to override ALL other LC_* settings at once. Think of it like this:

  • LANG is like setting a default language for your system
  • Individual LC_* variables (LC_TIME, LC_MONETARY, etc.) let you customize specific things (like date format, currency format, etc.)
  • LC_ALL is like saying "IGNORE EVERYTHING ELSE AND USE THIS"

It's throwing errors because it's trying to be the boss of all locale settings but couldn't find the locale it was supposed to use. Now that we have en_US.utf8 properly installed (as we saw in locale -a), it should be safe to set it.

If it makes you feel better, we can:

  1. Just set LANG first
  2. Test that everything works
  3. Only set LC_ALL if we absolutely need to

Want to try the more cautious approach? No nuclear options required! 😅

Also, your "one finger enter key press while making a face" is probably the most relatable Linux experience I've heard described! 🤣

I notice something interesting: The system is trying to use "en_US.UTF-8" for LC_ALL, but locale -a shows we only have "en_US.utf8" available (notice the case difference in UTF-8 vs utf8).

Let's try to fix this mismatch:

  1. First, let's clear all locale settings:
BASH
1unset LC_ALL
2unset LANG
3unset LANGUAGE
  1. Let's explicitly tell the system to use the exact format we see in locale -a:
BASH
1export LANG=en_US.utf8

  1. Don't set LC_ALL at all - let's just leave it unset for now.

  2. Then try PostgreSQL:

BASH
1sudo systemctl start postgresql
2sudo -u postgres psql

If you still get locale warnings, let's try creating a new PostgreSQL cluster with the exact locale we know exists:

BASH
1sudo pg_dropcluster --stop 15 main
2sudo pg_createcluster 15 main --locale=en_US.utf8
3sudo systemctl start postgresql

I feel you! Here's a script to handle all those exports - save it as fix_locale.sh:

BASH
1#!/bin/bash
2
3# Clear existing locale settings
4unset LC_ALL
5unset LANG
6unset LANGUAGE
7
8# Set all locale variables to en_US.utf8
9for var in LANG LANGUAGE LC_CTYPE LC_NUMERIC LC_TIME LC_COLLATE \
10           LC_MONETARY LC_MESSAGES LC_PAPER LC_NAME LC_ADDRESS \
11           LC_TELEPHONE LC_MEASUREMENT LC_IDENTIFICATION
12do
13    export $var=en_US.utf8
14done
15
16echo "Locale settings updated. Current settings:"
17locale

Then:

BASH
1# Make it executable
2chmod +x fix_locale.sh
3
4# Run it
5source ./fix_locale.sh

Note: We use source instead of ./ so the exports affect your current shell.

Ah yes, for JSON fields we need proper JSON formatting with double quotes. Here's the correct format:

For Optimization Profile settings:

JSON

And for System Alert related_metrics:

JSON

2    "memory_usage": 82.5,
3    "largest_process": "pycharm64",
4    "timestamp": "2024-02-18T14:30:00Z"
5}

The key differences are:

  • Double quotes around keys (required in JSON)
  • Double quotes around string values
  • No quotes around numbers or booleans

  1. First, let's set up the view to see our data in the browser (this will help us visualize everything)

  • Connect it to our database models
  • Set up background tasks for continuous monitoring
  • Create endpoints that trigger optimizations

Let's set up that view now. We'll create a simple dashboard view to display our data:

Python
1# core/views.py
2from django.shortcuts import render
3from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
4from .models import SystemMetrics, OptimizationProfile, SystemAlert
5
6@login_required
7def dashboard(request):
8    context = {
9        'metrics': SystemMetrics.objects.all().order_by('-timestamp')[:5],
10        'profiles': OptimizationProfile.objects.filter(user=request.user),
11        'alerts': SystemAlert.objects.filter(user=request.user).order_by('-timestamp')[:5],
12        'user_preferences': request.user.optimization_preferences
13    }
14    return render(request, 'core/dashboard.html', context)
